articles.title: Elon Musk advierte sobre el avance de la IA: “Podría superar a la inteligencia humana en cinco años”
articles.text:
Elon Musk volvió a lanzar una de sus predicciones más contundentes sobre el futuro de la inteligencia artificial: la tecnología podría superar la suma de la inteligencia humana en aproximadamente cinco años. El empresario considera que este avance podría transformar por completo el empleo, la economía y la capacidad de las personas para mantener el control sobre las máquinas.
“La IA podría superar la suma de la inteligencia humana en unos cinco años”, afirmó Musk en una entrevista con The Economist. El dueño de Tesla y SpaceX planteó un escenario en el que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial llegarían a desempeñar prácticamente cualquier tarea mejor que los seres humanos.
PUBLICIDAD
“No habrá nada que la IA no pueda hacer mejor que las personas, salvo, quizá, el hecho de ser humano”, añadió.
Para Musk, el avance tecnológico podría provocar un cambio sin precedentes en la posición de las personas dentro de la sociedad. El empresario incluso comparó la posible diferencia entre humanos e inteligencia artificial con la existente entre personas y chimpancés.
PUBLICIDAD
“Si la diferencia de inteligencia entre la inteligencia artificial y los humanos es mucho mayor que la que existe entre personas y chimpancés, cuesta imaginar que los monos sigan al mando”, señaló.
Musk anticipa el fin del trabajo como obligación
La proyección del empresario parte de la posibilidad de que la inteligencia artificial alcance un nivel capaz de realizar la mayoría de las actividades que actualmente dependen de las personas.
PUBLICIDAD
En ese escenario, el trabajo podría dejar de ser una obligación económica para convertirse en una actividad elegida por interés personal o satisfacción. Las personas seguirían trabajando, pero no necesariamente porque una empresa o profesión sea imprescindible para obtener ingresos.
Esta transformación, sin embargo, plantea una pregunta más compleja: qué ocurrirá con la capacidad de los seres humanos para tomar decisiones y controlar sistemas cada vez más inteligentes.
PUBLICIDAD
Musk describió el futuro de la inteligencia artificial como una tecnología que le genera sensaciones opuestas. Por un lado, considera que sus avances pueden abrir posibilidades extraordinarias. Por otro, reconoce que la velocidad del desarrollo puede producir riesgos difíciles de controlar.
El concepto de “singularidad” aparece en el centro de esta discusión. Se trata de una idea utilizada para describir un momento hipotético en el que las máquinas superan ampliamente las capacidades intelectuales humanas y su evolución tecnológica comienza a acelerarse de forma difícil de predecir.
PUBLICIDAD
Una propuesta de vigilancia entre las empresas de IA
Frente a estos riesgos, Musk propuso un modelo basado en la cooperación y la vigilancia mutua entre las principales empresas dedicadas a desarrollar inteligencia artificial.
Su planteamiento consiste en que los grandes laboratorios mantengan conversaciones periódicas sobre seguridad y compartan preocupaciones antes de lanzar modelos significativamente más avanzados.
Según Musk, antes de poner en circulación un nuevo sistema de inteligencia artificial que sea mucho más potente que los existentes, las empresas competidoras deberían tener la oportunidad de probarlo y buscar posibles comportamientos perjudiciales.
PUBLICIDAD
El empresario considera que este tipo de pruebas privadas podría ayudar a detectar riesgos antes de que un modelo sea lanzado de manera generalizada.
Musk argumentó que una revisión de aproximadamente una semana podría ser suficiente para realizar este tipo de evaluaciones. Su propuesta está inspirada, según explicó, en conversaciones que mantuvo con Demis Hassabis, uno de los principales referentes del sector de la inteligencia artificial.
PUBLICIDAD
El magnate también mostró dudas sobre la capacidad de los gobiernos para supervisar por sí solos estos sistemas. Considera que las autoridades pueden tener dificultades para seguir el ritmo de una tecnología que cambia rápidamente y requiere conocimientos técnicos especializados.
China, Estados Unidos y la carrera por la inteligencia artificial
La entrevista también abordó la competencia entre Estados Unidos y China, los dos principales protagonistas de la carrera global por la inteligencia artificial.
Musk considera que China tiene posibilidades reales de convertirse en líder de esta industria. Para el empresario, el desarrollo de modelos avanzados depende principalmente de dos recursos: chips y electricidad.
PUBLICIDAD
“Las limitaciones de la IA son, básicamente, la electricidad y los chips”, afirmó.
Estados Unidos mantiene restricciones sobre la exportación de determinados chips avanzados hacia China, pero Musk considera que el país asiático podría avanzar hacia una mayor autonomía tecnológica.
El empresario también destacó la capacidad de generación eléctrica de China, un factor que considera decisivo para alimentar los grandes centros de datos necesarios para entrenar y ejecutar sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
En este contexto, Musk cuestionó algunas prohibiciones sobre el uso de modelos desarrollados en China. Según su argumento, impedir que empresas estadounidenses utilicen determinados sistemas no significa que el resto del mundo vaya a dejar de utilizarlos.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Difficulties reveal the strength & character within a person
articles.text:
Difficulties reveal the strength & character within a person
Discover how difficulties reveal true character, build resilience, and shape personal growth through life's toughest challenges.
"Difficulties are things that show a person what they are." This powerful quote reminds us that our true nature is often revealed not during moments of comfort, but during times of struggle. When life is smooth, it is easy to appear patient, confident, and strong. However, when challenges arise, they test our values, resilience, and determination. Difficulties have a unique way of uncovering strengths we never knew we possessed while also highlighting areas where we need to grow.
Every successful individual, inspiring leader, and resilient person has faced hardships. Their achievements are not defined by the absence of difficulties but by how they responded to them. Challenges do more than create obstacles; they reveal character, build wisdom, and shape the person we become.
Difficulties reveal true character
A person's character is most visible when circumstances become challenging. Anyone can remain calm and positive when everything is going according to plan. However, setbacks, failures, and disappointments reveal how someone truly handles pressure.
When faced with difficulties, some people choose perseverance, honesty, and patience. Others may react with frustration or give up. These moments become opportunities to discover personal values and strengths. Challenges act like a mirror, showing us who we are beneath the surface.
Challenges uncover hidden strengths
Many people underestimate their abilities until they are forced to face a difficult situation. A challenging experience often pushes individuals beyond their comfort zones and helps them discover talents, courage, and resilience they never realised they had.
Someone who loses a job may discover entrepreneurial skills. A student struggling with exams may learn discipline and determination. A person facing personal loss may develop emotional strength that inspires others. Difficulties frequently reveal capabilities that remain hidden during easier times.
Growth happens through adversity
Personal growth rarely comes from comfort. Most valuable life lessons are learned through experiences that test patience, endurance, and adaptability. Difficult situations encourage people to think differently, solve problems creatively, and become more resilient.
Just as muscles grow stronger through resistance, character develops through challenges. Every obstacle teaches something valuable, whether it is patience, humility, courage, or persistence. These lessons often become the foundation for future success.
Difficulties teach resilience
Resilience is the ability to recover from setbacks and continue moving forward despite obstacles. It is one of the most important qualities a person can develop, and it is built through experience rather than theory.
Each challenge faced and overcome strengthens a person's ability to handle future difficulties. Over time, individuals learn that setbacks are temporary and that perseverance often leads to growth. Resilience transforms difficulties from barriers into stepping stones.
Failure often reveals potential
Many people view failure as a sign of weakness, but failure often reveals untapped potential. Some of the world's greatest achievements were preceded by repeated setbacks. What separates successful individuals from others is their willingness to learn from failure rather than be defeated by it.
Difficulties force people to evaluate their approach, improve their skills, and develop greater determination. In this way, failure becomes a powerful teacher that helps reveal what a person is capable of achieving.
Hardships create empathy and wisdom
People who have faced struggles often develop a deeper understanding of others. Difficult experiences can make individuals more compassionate, patient, and supportive because they understand what it feels like to face adversity.
Wisdom is rarely gained through easy experiences alone. It often comes from navigating uncertainty, making mistakes, and overcoming challenges. These experiences help people see life from a broader perspective and appreciate both success and hardship.
The importance of mindset during difficulties
While challenges are unavoidable, how a person responds to them is a choice. Viewing difficulties as opportunities for growth rather than obstacles can completely change their impact. A positive and determined mindset helps individuals find lessons in setbacks and strength in adversity.
People who embrace challenges often emerge stronger, wiser, and more confident. They understand that difficulties are temporary, but the qualities developed through them can last a lifetime.
Why this quote matter
The quote, "Difficulties are things that show a person what they are," captures a profound truth about human growth. Challenges reveal character, uncover hidden strengths, teach resilience, and provide valuable life lessons. While difficulties are rarely welcome, they often become the experiences that shape us most deeply.
Rather than fearing hardships, we can view them as opportunities to discover our true potential. In the end, it is not the difficulties themselves that define us, but how we choose to face them.

articles.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max launch with a familiar design, new A20 Pro SoC, and aperture-controlled camera
articles.text:
Through the looking glass: A new camera with the first-ever aperture controls on an iPhone is the main star of this year's iPhone presentation. With the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple is introducing a more versatile camera, more powerful photo-customization software, and yet another tech giant's attempt to distinguish authentic images from AI-generated creations.
Pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max open on September 12, with availability beginning September 18 starting at $1,199. As previously rumored, Apple seems to have delayed the standard iPhone 18 until next year.
The iPhone 18 Pro is the first iPhone to support aperture control. With six blades and a new sensor, users can smoothly switch between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0 apertures to control lighting and depth of field, as well as enhance low-light photography.
Users can also apply new texture styles and cinematic effects to videos recorded at up to 60fps. Additionally, time-lapse mode now supports 4K and Dolby Vision HDR recording. Meanwhile, the new iPhone adjusts the Dynamic Island to show up to three Live Activities simultaneously while still enabling Face ID.
Like Google and other developers, Apple also aims to provide a tool for watermarking AI-edited photos and verifying unaltered images. Apple Reference Image creates a duplicate of each new photo with cloud-processed, signed sensor data to prevent editing. Users can compare it with the copy they normally use to check for changes. A new API also makes reference images available to third-party apps, but the feature's resilience against ever-evolving AI tools in the wild remains untested.
The processor in this year's iPhone also receives another die shrink. The A20 Pro features TSMC's new 2-nanometer process, increasing memory bandwidth by 50% and GPU performance by 40% over the iPhone 17 Pro's A19 Pro. A new dual 16-core Neural Engine also enhances photography and AI performance, powering the iPhone 18's new photo features and iOS 27's AI-powered Siri.
A new vapor chamber improves thermal performance by 40%, while a new battery design extends the iPhone 18 Pro's maximum battery life to 36 hours and the iPhone 18 Pro Max's to 45 hours. The standard model can charge to 50% in approximately 15 minutes via a wired connection or 30 minutes wirelessly.
Storage options include 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and a new 2TB tier. Available colors include burgundy, glacier, silver, and black.

articles.title: AirPods 5 : Apple dévoile ses nouveaux écouteurs sans fil
articles.text:
Il y a deux ans, Apple levait le voile sur deux modèles d’AirPods 4, dont un avec réduction de bruit active. Un an plus tard, le constructeur sortait ses AirPods Pro 3. Aujourd’hui, la marque à la pomme profite de sa conférence « Surprise and Shine » pour lever le voile sur ses AirPods 5, qui arrivent en deux modèles. Voici tout ce que vous devez savoir sur les nouveaux écouteurs sans fil d’Apple.
Apple présente deux nouveaux modèles d’AirPods 5
Les AirPods 4 laissent leur place à deux modèles d’AirPods 5, toujours avec une forme ouverte « open ear » (pas d’embout en silicone dans l’oreille). Cette année, la particularité est que la réduction active du bruit (ANC) est disponible sur les deux modèles et qu’elle est 50 % plus efficace que sur la génération précédente.
Le mode transparence est également de la partie pour entendre les sons qui vous entourent et les deux modèles peuvent passer automatiquement de ce mode à la réduction du bruit en fonction des sons environnants grâce à l’audio adaptatif. Apple a également mis l’accent sur le fait que les AirPods 5 sont une des portes d’entrée vers Siri IA pour poser des questions et obtenir des réponses sans avoir à sortir votre iPhone. La traduction en direct, annoncée à l’automne dernier, est également de la partie. Apple affirme également avoir renforcé la durabilité de ses écouteurs à l’eau, à la poussière et à la transpiration.
La première version des AirPods 5 promet 4 h d’autonomie avec réduction du bruit activée et jusqu’à 20 h avec le boîtier.
Le second modèle profite de quelques petits trucs en plus, comme la possibilité de contrôler le volume sur la tige des écouteurs, comme sur les AirPods Pro 3. Il comprend également un chargeur sans fil et promet 5 h d’autonomie avec l’ANC activée.
© Apple
Prix et date de sortie des nouveaux AirPods 5
Les AirPods 5 seront disponibles le 22 septembre 2026 avec de la réduction de bruit active en standard, donc. Le modèle de base est proposé au même prix que le précédent et le second modèle avec le boîtier de recharge est proposé 30 € de moins que le prix des AirPods 4 avec Réduction active du bruit.
- AirPods 4 : 149 €
- AirPods 4 avec Réduction active du bruit : 199 €
- AirPods 5 : 149 €
- AirPods 5 avec Boîtier de charge sans fil : 169 €
- AirPods Pro 3 : 249 €

articles.title: “Él fue diseñado para obedecer, yo no”: hija de Elon Musk destrozó robots parodias de Tesla en una nueva campaña de moda
articles.text:
Vivian Wilson protagoniza la campaña Born to Disobey de Desigual con una secuencia en la que golpea, arrastra y utiliza como objeto a un robot de apariencia similar a los humanoides de Tesla. La hija distanciada de Elon Musk acompaña las imágenes con una frase que resume el mensaje de la pieza: “Él fue diseñado para obedecer, yo no”.
La campaña sitúa a la joven de 22 años frente a una representación de la IA y la robótica que remite al universo empresarial de su padre. Aunque se trata de una promoción de moda, el video utiliza esa relación para abordar asuntos como autonomía, obediencia y control tecnológico, en medio de la exposición pública que ha tenido Wilson desde su ruptura familiar.
PUBLICIDAD
Vivian Wilson se burla de los robots de Tesla
Desigual presentó la campaña con la intención de plantear que la rebelión actual puede consistir en negarse a formar parte de un sistema. La producción está dirigida por PSG, el colectivo formado por Yukihiro “Sho” Shoda, Pau López y Gerardo del Hierro, antes conocido como TURBO.
En una de las secuencias, Wilson usa el robot como soporte para practicar golf, lo lleva con una correa y trata de enseñarle a pronunciar el nombre de la marca. La máquina se avería de manera repetida, lo que lleva a la protagonista a decir: “Hay cosas que no están hechas para arreglarse”.
PUBLICIDAD
La campaña no identifica al robot como un producto de Tesla, pero sus rasgos visuales remiten a los humanoides que desarrolla la compañía del magnate sudafricano. Esa asociación convierte la pieza en una crítica simbólica a la idea de que la tecnología debe responder de forma automática a las órdenes de quien la controla.
La relación con Elon Musk permanece distante
Vivian Wilson se declaró transgénero en 2020 y, dos años después, cambió legalmente su nombre. En ese trámite dejó de utilizar el apellido Musk y adoptó Wilson, el apellido de su madre, Justine Wilson. También expresó que no quería mantener vínculo con su padre.
PUBLICIDAD
La distancia entre ambos se profundizó por las declaraciones de Musk sobre identidad de género y políticas de inclusión trans. Mientras el empresario ha difundido críticas sobre estos asuntos, Vivian se ha consolidado como una figura pública dentro de la comunidad LGTBIQ+ y ha construido una presencia propia en redes sociales, campañas y pasarelas.
En una entrevista reciente con Cosmopolitan, Wilson afirmó que la relación con su padre “es parte de mi historia, pero no define mi futuro”. También habló sobre haber crecido en una familia con grandes recursos económicos y sobre la forma en que el dinero puede transformar a las personas.
PUBLICIDAD
La modelo cuestionó la relación entre riqueza y poder
Wilson ha explicado que vio de cerca cómo el deseo de acumular poder puede afectar a una persona. “Lograr eso y querer más es un ciclo interminable de codicia y gula”, afirmó. Para la joven, el temor a convertirse en alguien distinto forma parte de una preocupación personal que aparece reflejada en su proyección pública.
La elección de Desigual la ubica en una campaña que no presenta la tecnología como un enemigo abstracto. El robot funciona como una figura que cumple órdenes, falla y carece de autonomía. Frente a él, Wilson plantea una posición de resistencia que conecta con su propia decisión de apartarse del apellido y la influencia de Musk.
PUBLICIDAD
El documental sobre Musk reaviva otros conflictos familiares
La campaña coincide con la atención generada por Musk, el documental de Alex Gibney que tendrá una proyección especial en el Festival Internacional de Cine de Venecia y llegará el 16 de octubre de 2026. La producción revisa el poder empresarial, político y tecnológico del dueño de Tesla, SpaceX y X.
Entre los testimonios figura Ashley St. Clair, madre de uno de los hijos de Musk. Ella afirmó que rechazó una oferta de 40 millones de dólares, más pagos mensuales de 100.000 dólares, para firmar un acuerdo de confidencialidad sobre su relación y el hijo que tuvieron en 2024.
PUBLICIDAD
St. Clair también cuestionó la actividad de X y sostuvo que la plataforma fomenta una división deliberada con consecuencias fuera de internet. Sus palabras, sumadas al mensaje de Vivian Wilson en la campaña de Desigual, muestran cómo las disputas alrededor de Musk trascienden sus empresas y alcanzan su vida familiar, su discurso público y la influencia de sus plataformas.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Apple dévoile les iPhone 18 Pro, deux nouveaux monstres de puissance et d'endurance
articles.text:
Lors de la keynote, Apple a dévoilé une nouvelle génération d’iPhone haut de gamme, composée de deux modèles, l’iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. Selon la marque, c’est évidemment « le meilleur iPhone Pro jamais conçu ». Contrairement aux années précédentes, Apple n’accompagne pas ses deux téléphones premium d’une édition standard plus abordable. Aucun iPhone 18 standard n’a été présenté lors de la keynote. Par contre, Apple a dévoilé l’iPhone Duo, son tout premier iPhone avec un écran pliant.
À lire aussi : AirPods 5 – voici les deux nouveaux modèles d’écouteurs sans fil d’Apple
Un design qui évolue… un peu
Sur le plan du design, Apple a opté pour une évolution plutôt qu’une révolution. Le châssis reprend globalement celui de l’iPhone 17 Pro, avec le même bloc photo proéminent à l’arrière. En fait, le changement visuel le plus visible se situe en haut de l’écran. La Dynamic Island, l’îlot qui dissimule les capteurs de reconnaissance faciale, a rétréci, laissant plus de place pour l’affichage. Côté coloris, Apple mise sur du noir, de l’argent, du bleu glacier, et du bordeaux. Sans surprise, le bordeaux est la grande couleur de l’année.
L’iPhone 18 Pro est recouvert d’un écran OLED de 6,3 pouces, avec taux de rafraîchissement adaptatif ProMotion jusqu’à 120 Hz. Plus imposant, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max hérite d’un écran de 6,9 pouces. Pas de surprise de ce côté-là !
Un appareil photo jamais vu chez Apple
La grande nouveauté de l’iPhone 18 Pro se trouve côté photo. L’iPhone 18 Pro inaugure l’ouverture variable sur son objectif principal. C’est une première chez Apple. Un système mécanique ajuste désormais l’ouverture du diaphragme pour mieux maîtriser la profondeur de champ. Six petites lamelles en composite, taillées au laser, s’ouvrent ou se referment devant le capteur comme le ferait l’iris d’un œil. Le triple module reste composé d’un capteur principal, d’un téléobjectif et d’un ultra grand-angle, tous en 48 mégapixels.
Pour Greg Joswiak, le responsable du marketing d’Apple, ce nouvel appareil photo « permet à tous de prendre facilement des photos et des vidéos exceptionnelles grâce à l’ouverture variable, tout en offrant une plus grande polyvalence aux créateurs et un contrôle accru aux professionnels ». Comme toujours, Apple présente son iPhone Pro comme le smartphone idéal pour les créateurs, les photographes et les vidéastes. Les professionnels bénéficient particulièrement de l’ouverture variable, puisqu’ils peuvent ajuster manuellement les quatre paliers d’ouverture directement depuis l’application Appareil photo, détaille Apple.
La puissance de la puce A20 Pro
Sous le capot, la nouvelle puce A20 Pro est gravée en 2 nanomètres par TSMC. Là encore, c’est une première pour Apple. C’est la même finesse de gravure que celle utilisée pour la puce Apple M6. Le géant de Cupertino annonce un gain de performances plutôt conséquent. La nouvelle puce Apple A20 Pro embarque un GPU à sept cœurs, promettant jusqu’à 40% de gains de performances comparé à l’A19 Pro. Côté processeur, l’A20 Pro compte six cœurs CPU au total : deux “super cœurs” haute performance et quatre cœurs plus économes en énergie. Apple affirme que ces deux gros cœurs sont, de loin, les plus rapides de toute l’industrie du semi-conducteur. La bande passante mémoire de l’A20 Pro progresse de 50%.
Le moteur neuronal de l’A20 Pro a lui aussi été revu, avec l’ajout de deux modules supplémentaires, portant le total à 32 cœurs. Cette évolution permet de doubler les performances dédiées à l’intelligence artificielle. C’est évidemment l’idéal pour faire tourner Apple Intelligence, la suite d’outils IA du groupe, au cœur de la keynote, ainsi que le nouveau Siri AI, également au centre de la conférence. Comme prévu, Apple a amélioré le système de refroidissement. Ce système améliore considérablement les performances de l’iPhone en dissipant mieux la chaleur. L’écran a également été repensé pour bénéficier d’un refroidissement plus efficace.
L’autonomie en forte hausse
Apple en profite aussi pour gonfler l’autonomie de ses iPhone. En partie grâce à la puce A20 Pro, moins énergivore, les smartphones devraient jouir d’une autonomie de plus d’une journée, similaire à l’iPhone 17 Pro Max, en dépit d’une batterie plus petite. Apple précise que l’iPhone 18 Pro tient 24 heures en usage quotidien classique sur une seule charge, contre 30 heures pour la version Max, qui bénéficie d’une plus grosse batterie. C’est la « plus forte augmentation d’autonomie jamais réalisée sur iPhone ». Apple a également amélioré la charge rapide de ses nouveaux iPhone. Il suffit désormais de 15 minutes de charge pour récupérer 50% de batterie.
Prix et date de sortie des iPhone 18 Pro
Comme on le craignait, Apple a considérablement revu à la hausse le prix de l’iPhone Pro d’une année à l’autre. La marque californienne propose l’iPhone 18 Pro au prix de départ de 1 479 €. De son côté, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max est commercialisé au prix de départ de 1629 euros. Sans plus attendre, voici tous les prix en vigueur en France :
- iPhone 18 Pro 256 Go : 1 479 €
- iPhone 18 Pro 512 Go : 1 729 €
- iPhone 18 Pro 1 To : 2 229 €
- iPhone 18 Pro 2 To : 2 979 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 256 Go : 1 629 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 512 Go : 1 879 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 1 To : 2 379 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 2 To : 3 129 €
Fait inhabituel, Apple a décalé le calendrier de ses précommandes. Plutôt que d’ouvrir les précommandes le traditionnel vendredi suivant l’annonce, les précommandes ouvriront le samedi 12 septembre 2026. Ce changement permet d’éviter une ouverture des précommandes le 11 septembre, date du 25ᵉ anniversaire des attentats de 2001. Les nouveaux iPhone seront disponibles en magasin à partir du 18 septembre 2026. Allez-vous craquer pour cette nouvelle génération ? On attend votre avis dans les commentaires.

Dear Reader,
India has ordered action against 15 offshore crypto platforms for allegedly operating in the country without complying with its anti-money laundering framework. The Financial Intelligence Unit-India has issued non-compliance notices to platforms including Weex, Blofin, Bitunix, DigiFinex, Toobit, XT.com, WOO X and Pionex, and sought the takedown of their apps and websites. Offshore virtual digital asset service providers are required to register with FIU-IND and comply with reporting obligations under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
Primary market demand surged on Wednesday as six IPOs launched simultaneously, with Rentomojo, Karamtara Engineering, and LCC Projects all getting fully subscribed on day one.
The Rs 1,256-crore IPO of Rentomojo attracted bids for 3.08 crore shares against 2.18 crore shares on offer, translating into a subscription of 1.42 times. The online furniture and appliance rental platform has fixed a price band of Rs 384-404 per equity share, PTI reported.
Meanwhile, fintech company BharatPe is doubling down on AI. At the Global Fintech Fest 2026, the company launched two new tools: BharatPe Agentic AI, an AI assistant for merchants, and Credit Coach, which leverages AI to increase credit awareness among users.
Elsewhere, Meta has unveiled Muse, a personal AI agent built to execute multi-step tasks across websites and connected services autonomously, marking a shift from passive QA models to proactive, unsupervised AI.
While tech companies are rolling out new tools that purportedly make our lives easier, a former AI researcher has sounded an alarm bell over AI development.
AI researcher Jacob Coxon has resigned from Anthropic, following three years of pretraining research across OpenAI and Anthropic. He has warned that leading laboratories are recklessly prioritising rapid technological progress over human safety.
“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible - but I hear the same people express fear privately,” he said.

Funding
Private equity firm Motilal Oswal’s PPE bet
Private equity firm Motilal Oswal Alternates has invested Rs 600 crore ($63 million) in KARAM Safety, one of India's leading occupational safety solutions and personal protective equipment (PPE) manufacturers. The deal marks the fifth deployment from Motilal Oswal’s Rs 8,500 crore India Business Excellence Fund V (IBEF V).
Founded in 1998, KARAM Safety will use the capital infusion to bolster product R&D, expand manufacturing capacities, and pursue strategic inorganic acquisitions across global markets.
Key Takeaways:
- The Rs 600 crore investment provides KARAM Safety with financial leverage to execute an aggressive growth and product diversification strategy.
- Funds will primarily target strategic acquisitions in complementary product categories and international markets, alongside expanding distribution across the US, Europe, LATAM, Africa, and Asia-Pacific.
- The deal underscores growing private equity interest in industrial safety and specialised manufacturing, driven by stricter global safety regulations, sustained industrial capex, and India's rising footprint as a high-quality manufacturing hub.

Samtel Avionics, and Japan’s BULL Co team up on space debris
Indian defence and aerospace manufacturer Samtel Avionics has signed a memorandum of understanding with Japanese space-tech startup BULL Co., Ltd. to explore combining passive post-mission disposal (PMD) technologies with active debris removal systems.
The partnership aims to develop practical, scalable solutions for space sustainability by addressing both prevention (ensuring operational satellites de-orbit upon retirement) and active remediation (removing legacy debris). The move highlights Samtel Avionics' broader expansion from traditional defence avionics into satellite systems and advanced spacetech.
Space race:
- The agreement is exploratory rather than a commitment to a commercial product, but it points to a broader shift in the space industry towards tackling debris both before and after satellites stop operating.
- The European Space Agency estimates that about 40,000 objects are currently tracked in Earth orbit, including roughly 11,000 active payloads.
- Under the MoU, the companies will examine technical requirements, system interfaces, customisation and possible integration.

articles.title: iPhone Duo pliant, iPhone 18 Pro, AirPods 5 et Siri AI : le bilan de toutes les annonces Apple
articles.text:
iPhone Duo pliant, iPhone 18 Pro, AirPods 5 et Siri AI : le bilan de toutes les annonces Apple
La grande messe annuelle d'Apple vient tout juste de se conclure au Steve Jobs Theater de Cupertino. Pour sa keynote de rentrée ce 9 septembre 2026, la firme à la pomme a frappé fort en officialisant son très attendu tout premier smartphone pliant, l'iPhone Duo, aux côtés des iPhone 18 Pro, des AirPods 5 et des Apple Watch Series 12.
Entre innovations matérielles majeures, ajustements tarifaires et annonces cruciales autour du déploiement de Siri AI — qui réserve d'ailleurs une mauvaise surprise aux utilisateurs européens —, voici le récapitulatif complet de tout ce qu'il fallait retenir de la conférence.
iPhone Duo : le tout premier iPhone pliant à plus de 2 000 €
Clou du spectacle de la conférence, le premier smartphone pliant d'Apple se nomme iPhone Duo. Adoptant un format passeport, l'appareil arbore un écran intérieur de 7,6 pouces sans encoche grâce à l'intégration d'une caméra sous l'écran, le tout protégé par du Ceramic Shield et une structure renforcée en titane certifiée IP68. Équipé de la puce A20 Pro, le Duo embarque deux batteries pour égaler l'autonomie des modèles Pro et se démarque par la prise en charge du stylet Apple Pencil sur ses deux écrans ainsi que par un double module photo de 48 Mpx.
Côté logiciel, l'interface Liquid Glass tire parti du format avec un mode "flex" pour la visioconférence ou le chevet, du multifenêtrage et des raccourcis repensés pour l'usage à une main. Positionné sur le très haut de gamme pour concurrencer le Galaxy Z Fold 8, cet iPhone Ultra s'affiche au tarif musclé de 2 339 € (en version 256 Go). Il sera disponible en France un peu plus tard que les autres modèles, avec des précommandes ouvertes le 16 octobre et une commercialisation fixée au 23 octobre.
iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max : puissance, photo variable et prix en hausse
Inaugurant l'ère John Ternus, lesiPhone 18 Pro et Pro Maxconservent leur design avec un coloris Dark Cherry inédit et une Dynamic Island rétrécie, capable de gérer trois activités simultanées. Sous le capot, la nouvelle puce A20 Pro gravée en 2 nm double la puissance dédiée à l'IA tout en améliorant le refroidissement. Ce gain d'efficience permet d'atteindre jusqu'à 45 heures de lecture vidéo sur le Pro Max et d'offrir une recharge à 50 % en 15 minutes.
Côté photo, le capteur principal gagne une ouverture mécanique variable pour ajuster la profondeur de champ sans artifice logiciel, épaulée par des réglages Pro manuels intégrés à l'application native. Face au coût des composants, les tarifs grimpent de 100 $ : l'iPhone 18 Pro débute à 1 199 $ (256 Go) et le Pro Max à 1 299 $, en attendant la grille de prix en euros.
AirPods 5 : réduction de bruit pour tous et baisse de prix
Présentés plus tôt que prévu, les AirPods 5généralisent la réduction de bruit active (ANC) sur l'ensemble de la gamme. Désormais déclinés en deux versions toutes deux équipées de l'ANC, ces écouteurs ouverts promettent une isolation 50 % plus efficace grâce à une nouvelle architecture acoustique multiports et un mode Transparence plus naturel. Toujours propulsés par la puce H2, ils gagnent une certification IP57 pour une meilleure résistance à l'eau et à la poussière.
La déclinaison la plus évoluée se distingue par le contrôle du volume par balayage, une autonomie poussée à 5 heures d'écoute (contre 4 heures sur la version standard) et un boîtier compatible avec la charge sans fil Qi. Apple revoit ses tarifs à la baisse de 30 € sur le modèle d'entrée de gamme, affiché à 149 € (sans charge sans fil), tandis que la version supérieure avec boîtier Qi s'affiche à 169 €, avec une disponibilité prévue dès le 18 septembre.
Apple Watch Series 12 et Ultra 4 : IA, santé avancée et prix maintenus
Officialisées lors de la conférence, les Apple Watch Series 12 et Ultra 4intègrent la nouvelle puce S11 pour faire tourner watchOS 27 et ses fonctions d'IA. Parmi elles, Audio Intelligence permet d'analyser l'environnement sonore et de retranscrire à l'écran les 15 dernières secondes d'une conversation grâce à Live Rewind. Côté santé, l'application s'enrichit d'un score de récupération Préparation, d'un suivi de l'âge biologique et d'un test VO2 max via la caméra de l'iPhone, tandis que les capteurs au dos du boîtier gagnent en précision pour le suivi cardiaque et les ECG.
Sur le plan matériel, l'Ultra 4 pousse son autonomie au-delà des 48 heures, tandis que la Series 12 franchit la barre des 24 heures et gagne une protection Ceramic Shield en aluminium bronze, aux côtés du retour de la céramique en blanc ou bleu nuit. Bonne nouvelle pour le portefeuille : Apple conserve ses prix de départ à 449 € (399 $) pour la Series 12 et 899 € (799 $) pour l'Ultra 4, avec des précommandes ouvertes dès aujourd'hui pour des livraisons le 18 septembre.
Siri AI : la douche froide pour les utilisateurs européens
Très attendue, la refonte de Siri AI apporte une interactivité inédite avec la caméra de l'iPhone et des applications tierces comme WhatsApp ou Audible. Apple a confirmé l'arrivée de la fonction en anglais dès ce mois-ci en version bêta, puis en français, espagnol et portugais dès octobre 2026.
Cependant, le bras de fer réglementaire autour du Digital Markets Act (DMA) privera les smartphones européens de cette avancée. Siri AI sera bien disponible en français dès le mois prochain, mais uniquement pour les utilisateurs situés hors de l'Union européenne. Dans la même logique, la fonction photo Apple Reference Image des iPhone 18 Pro boudera également le Vieux Continent.

articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12 y Ultra 4: el gran salto está en salud, pero ahora también pueden recordar lo que hemos hablado
articles.text:
Hay una enorme diferencia entre saber cuántas veces ha latido nuestro corazón y entender qué nos está diciendo ese dato. El Apple Watch lleva años acumulando información sobre nuestra actividad, sueño y salud, pero esta generación intenta reducir precisamente esa distancia entre medir e interpretar. Los nuevos Series 12 y Ultra 4 parten de una renovación profunda de sus sensores y de un chip preparado para trabajar con mucha más información durante todo el día. Y ahora el reloj también empieza a prestar atención a otra fuente de información que siempre hemos tenido alrededor al más puro estilo Plaud: nuestras conversaciones.
Apple ha presentado ambos modelos durante "Un rayo de wow.", la misma keynote que ha servido para enseñar los iPhone 18 Pro y 18 Pro Max y su primer teléfono plegable. El Series 12 continúa como el reloj pensado para un público más amplio, mientras que el Ultra 4 conserva su orientación hacia deporte, aventura y actividades prolongadas. Buena parte de la tecnología que los hace avanzar es compartida: Health Sensing System, chip S11 y una nueva capa de software que intenta convertir las señales recogidas durante el día en información que resulte más fácil utilizar.
Más datos, pero también más contexto
El nuevo sistema incorpora sensores cardiacos ópticos y eléctricos y unos LED verdes más grandes y eficientes. Gracias a ellos, el reloj mide la frecuencia cardiaca cada cinco segundos de forma pasiva durante todo el día y registra la variabilidad cardiaca hasta 24 veces más frecuentemente. Todo ello alimenta readiness, que cruza actividad reciente, carga de entrenamiento, constantes y puntuación de sueño para ofrecernos un valor entre 0 y 10 acompañado de una recomendación sobre cómo afrontar la jornada. No es una fotografía fija: el resultado puede actualizarse si nuestro estado o actividad cambian.
En el Series 12, Apple acompaña esa renovación interna con algunos cambios tangibles. Sigue disponible en 42 y 46 mm y recupera la caja de cerámica, desaparecida desde el Series 5, ahora en blanco perla y azul noche. Los modelos de aluminio incorporan Ceramic Shield 2, un material que la compañía cifra como un 60% más resistente que el Ion-X de la generación anterior. Sus 24 horas de autonomía cotidiana no cambian, pero los entrenamientos al aire libre alcanzan 10 horas y 15 minutos conectado permiten obtener hasta otras 12 horas de batería.
En el Ultra 4, la batería se convierte en una diferencia mucho más seria. El reloj alcanza ahora hasta 50 horas de uso normal y 84 horas en bajo consumo, además de sumar hasta 18 horas con una carga de 15 minutos. Para quienes realmente lo utilicen en actividades largas, Extended Workout ofrece hasta 25 horas manteniendo GPS y frecuencia cardiaca, mientras que Max Extended Workout eleva el registro hasta 45 horas con posiciones GPS cada segundo. La compañía mantiene así el planteamiento del Ultra como el reloj destinado a quienes necesitan llevar estas capacidades bastante más lejos.
El S11 abre además un camino que poco tiene que ver con contar pasos. Audio Intelligence utiliza el micrófono del reloj para reconocer sonidos y trabajar con nuestras conversaciones: con Siri Recap activado, Apple Watch puede generar automáticamente un título y varios puntos clave cuando terminamos de hablar, mientras que Live Rewind recupera como texto los 15 segundos anteriores para consultar algo que acabamos de perder.
Somos nosotros quienes decidimos cuándo utiliza estas funciones y Apple afirma que el sistema no almacena grabaciones, porque el audio bruto se procesa en un entorno aislado del chip y se elimina inmediatamente. Se trata de una solución interesante, aunque probablemente también despertará preguntas acerca de privacidad. Siri Recap y Live Rewind llegarán en beta más adelante y, alto muy importante, no estarán disponibles inicialmente en la Unión Europea.
Precio y disponibilidad
Apple ha abierto las reservas de ambos relojes y su llegada a tiendas está prevista para el 18 de septiembre. El Apple Watch Series 12 cuesta desde 449 euros en España, mientras que el Apple Watch Ultra 4 parte de 899 euros.

articles.title: La fin de l'humain ? Xpeng lance une ligne production de son robot Iron... à 80% automatisée
articles.text:
On avance à toute vitesse du côté des robots en Chine. Xpeng se met ainsi à produire son robot, avec très peu d'assistance humaine au programme !
La Chine, c'est le nouveau berceau des robots, où l'on produit tous types de machines de ce genre (comme les chiens robots). Et cette avance est saluée par les plus grands, comme encore Elon Musk au mois de novembre dernier au moment de la présentation du robot Iron, de l'entreprise Xpeng. Un robot qui entre cette semaine en production.
Xpeng met en service la ligne de production de son nouveau robot Iron, à 80% automatisée
Au début du mois de novembre dernier, le robot Iron de Xpeng avait impressionné par sa morphologie et sa démarche fluide, extrêmement proche de celle de l'être humain. Un robot dont la première ligne de production vient d'être officiellement mise en service.
Un passage en phase industrielle particulier, puisque selon la firme chinoise, cette ligne est à 80% automatisée. En somme, on se retrouve ici avec des automates qui produisent des robots, avec des humains relégués à une petite partie des tâches restantes. Petite illustration de ce découplage humain/robot, la vidéo de promotion, que vous pouvez retrouver ci-dessous, nous montre un robot qui quitte la ligne de production en marchant de manière autonome.
Optimus a-t-il du souci à se faire ?
Et Xpeng voudrait aller très vite sur ce produit, avec un lancement commercial en Chine et au niveau international programmé pour 2027. Pour rappel, e robot, d'une taille allant de 1,73 à 1,77 mètre et d'un poid de 70 kilos, possède des mains de 21 à 22 degrés de liberté (il peut se saisir d'un objet avec délicatesse, et aussi travailler avec de l'outillage industriel). Il intègre par ailleurs trois puces Turing délivrant une puissance de calcul impressionnante de 2 250 TOPS.
Cette sortie pourrait aussi permettre de comparer directement dans les prochaines années les avancées des deux concurrents chinois et américains. Car le robot Iron de Xpeng va rivaliser avec le fameux robot Optimus de Tesla, dont la production a commencé au mois d'août dernier sur l'ancienne ligne de Model S et Model X de l'usine de Fremont. Qui l'emportera à la fin ?

articles.title: Corsair made a $200 gaming chair and then tested it like it was going into battle
articles.text:
Gaming Comfort: Gaming chairs are often one of the most overlooked pieces of furniture in a gaming setup. While luxury "thrones" can be left to customers with truly deep pockets, most gamers should at least consider investing in a somewhat expensive chair to ease the discomfort that comes with long gaming sessions.
Corsair recently launched the TC80 Gaming Chair, a new armchair designed to provide a durable and comfortable seating option for PC-focused gaming setups. The Fremont-based corporation highlights how its new chair has undergone more than 30 durability and safety tests, suggesting that it should accommodate gamers with a wide range of body types.
The TC80 Gaming Chair meets the BIFMA X5.1 and EN 1335 standards for office chairs, Corsair said. The chair underwent a series of demanding durability, stability, and weight-load tests, with Corsair particularly proud of how its new product survived the onslaught.
These tests included dropping a 136kg load onto the center of the seat, applying a 1,001N load to the backrest for 60 seconds, and placing 13 heavy discs against the backrest. Furthermore, the chair survived 100,000 cycles of a 57kg weight falling onto the seat, 60,000 cycles of 400N being applied to each armrest, and 120,000 swivel-test cycles with 122kg placed on the seat at both its maximum and minimum height.
The TC80 Gaming Chair provides a "generously" wide and flat seat with plush padding, breathable fabric upholstery, and 100mm of adjustable seat height. There is even a detachable neck pillow for people who like to alternate between office work sessions and more relaxing activities. The chair's stability comes from a steel five-star base, 50mm casters, and a Class 4 steel gas lift that should last for years.
Talking about comfort, Corsair's new chair offers a recline range of 90° to 115°. Users can adjust and lock the chair at their preferred angle, so there is no need to settle for a fixed position straight out of the box.
Corsair is already selling the TC80 Gaming Chair through its own store and other major retailers. The chair costs $200 in the US, while customers in Europe and the UK can get it for €180 and £170, respectively. The company's official announcement provides a full list of regional launch prices.
Corsair also highlights the TC80 as an entry-level product in its growing lineup of gaming chairs. The company already offers more expensive models, such as the TC100 Relaxed and the premium TC500 Luxe.
The TC500 comes with a €550 price tag in Europe, which is still a relatively affordable purchase compared with some truly expensive chairs, such as the obscenely priced Herman Miller x Logitech Embody. For now, I think I'll stick with my cheap Songmics gaming chair.

articles.title: Lawsuit: Amazon refused to give pregnant workers bathroom breaks and chairs
articles.text:
Amazon discriminated against pregnant warehouse employees by denying accommodations like bathroom breaks and the option to sit while working, according to a lawsuit filed yesterday by four women who worked for Amazon while pregnant. The lawsuit is a class-action complaint that seeks to represent Amazon workers throughout the US.
“Plaintiffs Willamina Barclay, Kristina Green, Jennifer Hatch, and Dazaria Parks were formerly Amazon warehouse employees,” said the lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Eastern District of New York. “All four became pregnant. All four asked Amazon for basic pregnancy-related accommodations so they could keep doing their jobs. Amazon denied them basic modifications the law recognizes pregnant workers regularly need, even in uncomplicated pregnancies: Bathroom breaks. An extra 15-minute break. Sitting instead of standing.”
The lawsuit said the four plaintiffs were unlawfully terminated from jobs at Amazon facilities in New York between April 2025 and July 2026. After the plaintiffs “took medically necessary breaks or absences to get off their feet, visit the doctor, or go to the emergency room, they were punished,” the lawsuit said. “Amazon deducted their limited bank of unpaid time off. Soon enough, they had depleted that limited bank of ‘unpaid time off,’ and Amazon threatened to terminate them.”
In a statement, Amazon said the lawsuit contains inaccuracies and denied that it violates federal law on pregnancy accommodations. “We’re limited in discussing ongoing legal matters, however we look forward to a timely resolution of these matters, as extended investigation timelines benefit neither employees nor employers,” Amazon said.
Amazon has faced similar lawsuits in previous years, but this one has the added backing of a 2022 US law called the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA). The relatively new federal law requires “reasonable accommodations for qualified employees affected by pregnancy, childbirth, lactation, or related medical conditions and limitations so long as doing so does not create an undue hardship on the entity’s operations,” the lawsuit said.

articles.title: Massachusetts hits data centers with new clean power rules | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Massachusetts became the latest state to force data centers to bring their own power, but this time there’s a twist. A new state mandate would require developers building data centers larger than 25 megawatts to provide clean power or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.
Gov. Maura Healey’s executive order is the latest example of states turning against data centers. Just a few years ago, tech companies and data center developers were showered with incentives to locate facilities in a particular state. Now they’re fighting a groundswell of public opposition as politicians seek to show voters they’re addressing their concerns.
Under Healey’s order, data centers larger than 25 megawatts of peak demand will have to bring their own power and guarantee that it adheres to the state’s clean energy requirements. Healey would prefer that they generate the clean power on-site, too. If not, they’ll need to fund the construction of new generation nearby or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.
Massachusetts is also directing communities to “avoid signing non-disclosure agreements,” according to the executive order. To give regulators time to implement the new restrictions, the governor is pausing applications for a data center sales tax exemption that went into effect last month.
Healey said data centers must meet the Massachusetts clean energy standard enshrined in state law, although it comes with some added strength. The state’s clean energy standard dictates that industry only generate a portion of their power using approved sources like wind, solar, and hydro. In 2030, for example, those sources must contribute at least 40% of the total. The amount varies by year, and it ratchets up over time. But the governor’s office clarified that data centers will be required to meet 100% of its electricity demand with clean energy generation.
With the new restrictions, Massachusetts becomes the third state in as many months to rein in data center development.
In August, Texas governor Greg Abbott announced that all new data centers in the state would need to submit to audits by the public utility commission and the grid operator, ERCOT. In July, New York’s governor stopped construction of new data centers 50 megawatts or larger.
With public sentiment shifting against data centers, the tech industry is starting to push back. Pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future — which is funded by Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, and Greg Brockman — is buying ads that seek to sway voters in battleground states ahead of midterm elections.
Update: This article was updated with information from the Massachusetts governor’s office that clarified the executive order will require data centers to meet 100% of its electricity demand with clean energy generation.

Modular laptop manufacturer Framework has just announced that it's dropping some of its memory pricing for its new Framework Laptop 13 Pro after previously doubling it back in July, including retroactively for orders that have already shipped. Posting on social media and in an update on its blog, the company says that it's been able to source new inventory at a reduced cost.
"We have a positive update today on LPCAMM2 pricing! We were able to source a limited quantity at lower cost, and are retroactively reducing prices for orders that shipped at higher price, as well as offering the lower price to orders through Batch 10" according to the company's recent X post. A further update, posted on the company's blog, goes on to explain that Framework's Supply Chain team "has been working continuously to source additional inventory at better prices."
The lower prices are due to a "limited quantity" of Micron 32GB and 64GB LPCAMM2 memory modules that the company has secured at "lower cost," and that as the company is "committed to passing on savings whenever we can," it is passing the price reductions back to customers. LPCAMM2 memory is available for the Intel Core Ultra Series 3 version of the Framework laptop. Other models, like those shipping with AMD Ryzen AI 300 CPUs, are using SO-DIMMs instead.
The price reductions are being applied to "both already shipped and a subset of pending pre-orders," according to chief executive Nirav Patel. This improves the situation for consumers compared to the last price update on July 22, which saw Framework almost double its prices for 32GB and 64GB LPCAMM2 memory in the Laptop 13 Pro. While these new prices are "still above our original pre-order launch baseline, they are lower than the last cost update that drove our current pricing for new pre-orders," according to the company.
This pricing isn't expected to last for long, however. As Framework notes, only a limited quantity of new modules has been acquired at lower cost. Framework explains on X that these are being made available "first-come, first-serve to customers through Batch 10". If the company is able to source more, then it'll "open it to later batches and then to new pre-orders."
Framework is automatically refunding the difference if your order has already shipped and you paid the higher price. Pending pre-orders through to Batch 10 have also been adjusted to reflect the better pricing. If you're waiting on a pre-order and want to update the RAM capacity you've ordered to take advantage of the lower prices, that option is now available via the order summary page, with instructions in Framework's Help Center if you run into trouble.
Those with a DIY Edition Framework 13 Pro that has already shipped and who want to switch to the 32GB or 64GB LPCAMM2 modules at the lower price can also fill out this contact form to organize a swap.

articles.title: Your favorite app is silently collecting your browsing history, Surfshark warns
articles.text:
Your favorite app is silently collecting your browsing history, Surfshark warns
18 of 40 top apps collect your browsing history, and most of them do not need it
- Nearly half of the top mobile apps collect your browsing history
- Social media apps are the worst offenders
- Avoiding in-app browsers can limit data collection
You probably assume your web browser is the only app keeping tabs on where you go online. According to new research from Surfshark, that assumption is incorrect.
The cybersecurity firm analyzed 40 of the most popular Android and iOS apps and found that 18 of them, or 45%, report collecting users' browsing history in their app store privacy labels. In other words, nearly half of the apps you open every day may be logging the websites you visit.
Even the best VPN cannot fully stop an app from recording what you do inside its own walls, which makes understanding what you are signing up for more important than ever.
Surfshark – the best cheap VPN
Surfshark is a fast, easy-to-use VPN that seriously beats the competition when it comes to subscription pricing. Its two-year Starter plan works out at $2.49 a month (plus tax), but we think Surfshark One is the best value plan as it adds an antivirus, data breach monitor, and alternative ID tool starting from the equivalent of  $2.79 a month. 
What Surfshark found
Surfshark's team looked at 40 leading apps split evenly across four categories: generative AI, social media, e-commerce, and messaging.
For each one, the researchers checked whether its Apple App Store label reported collecting "Browsing History" and whether its Google Play label reported "Web Browsing History."
Social media came out as the biggest collector by far. Nine of the 10 social apps studied collect browsing history on at least one platform. Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, and Pinterest do so on both Android and iOS, while Reddit, LinkedIn, and Snapchat collect it on Android only. Discord was the only social app that collected it on neither.
E-commerce came next, with half of the shopping apps analyzed collecting the data on at least one platform.
Messaging was less hungry, with only Rakuten Viber, Messenger, and LINE gathering it, echoing earlier findings on how much data messaging apps collect.
In the generative AI category, Google Gemini was the only app of the 10 to report collecting browsing history.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Why apps want your browsing history
The logic is straightforward: the more an app knows about where you go online, the more precisely it can target ads and shape the content in your feed.
As Surfshark's lead system engineer Karolis Kaciulis explains, many apps now route external links through their own "embedded browsers," so the moment you tap a link, they can track what you search for and look at.
The important thing to remember here is that most of these social media and shopping apps do not need your browsing history to provide their services. The practice is not related to providing value to users, and simply takes place to benefit the app companies.
Kaciulis argues that consent for this is usually buried in the fine print, and that the apps fighting hardest to keep you inside their own browser tend to be the ones selling ads rather than the ones that need your history to function.
How to stay safe
There is no single switch that turns all of this off, but a few habits can go a long way.
The easiest is to sidestep in-app browsers: when you tap a link, use the "Open in default browser" option or paste the URL into your default browser, which stops the host app from watching where you go next.
Pair this with switching to a privacy-focused browser, and you'll be able to avoid a lot of the worst data-collecting practices without much effort.

articles.title: Orchid Security gives enterprises a kill switch for rogue AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Orchid Security gives enterprises a kill switch for rogue AI agents
Identity security startup Orchid Security Inc. today added identity drift detection and application-level kill switches for artificial intelligence agents to its Identity Control Plane.
The controls are meant to let security teams strip an agent of its authority the moment its behavior moves outside what was approved.
Agents rarely have to defeat a security control to exceed their intended scope, according to the company. They inherit the problem instead. Hard-coded credentials, dormant accounts and unmanaged authentication paths are already sitting across most enterprise application estates, and an agent working at machine speed can chain them into elevated access in seconds to minutes.
Orchid’s report “The Identity Gap: 2026 Snapshot,” published in May, found invisible identity outnumbering the visible kind 57% to 43%. Two-thirds of nonhuman accounts in that sample had been provisioned inside applications, out of view of identity and access management tooling.
Five capabilities are available now. Orchid tags applications, identities and access paths with an AI readiness status. Orphaned, dormant, over-permissioned and suspicious accounts are surfaced as hygiene findings. Drift detection runs continuously, comparing what an agent was built to do against what it is actually doing. Response is orchestrated through whatever identity and security tooling the customer already runs, and an audit generator documents the agent activity, the identity behind it, the drift detected and the action taken.
Those actions run from trimming permissions to revoking credentials, disconnecting tools or suspending a workflow. The application-level kill switch goes further, terminating the authority the agent operates through.
Roy Katmor, co-founder and chief executive of Orchid, tied the release to boardroom pressure. Boards have stopped asking whether AI will be adopted and started asking why it is not moving faster, he said, and security cannot answer with a blanket no. “AI transformation is exciting. Identity hygiene is not,” Katmor said.
Shannon Wilkinson, chief information officer and chief information security officer at Findlay Automotive Group Inc., said the dealership group is leaning heavily on agents to improve customer experience while trying to keep sight of what those identities can reach. “It honestly terrifies a lot of us,” she said.
Two integrations shipped alongside the release. A certified connector for Palo Alto Networks Inc.’s Idira identity security platform discovers privileged accounts Idira does not already manage and brings them under its control. The second streams Orchid’s identity telemetry into Splunk Enterprise Security for correlation and incident response.
Orchid last extended the Identity Control Plane for agents in May, mapping agents back to their originating identities and adding observability over delegation chains. SailPoint Technologies Inc. certified the company’s governance orchestration in September 2025. Team8 Capital and Intel Capital Inc. co-led a $36 million seed round for Orchid in January 2025.

articles.title: Apple’s new CEO is reviving a Steve Jobs strategy from 25 years ago | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple CEO John Ternus wants you to know that the iPhone isn’t going anywhere.
Ternus threw his weight behind the venerable device on Wednesday during his first keynote as CEO, placing it firmly at the center of Apple’s product strategy for the AI era.
“There’s no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone,” he said.
This contrasts with the approach taken by former CEO Tim Cook, who tried time and again to convince Wall Street that Apple was more than just the iPhone.
Ternus’ pitch is also a rebuttal to pundits who have recently cast doubt on the iPhone. “The smartphone’s days are numbered,” said one headline. “The Tim Cook era is coming to a close with an existential challenge for Apple: figuring out what comes after the iPhone,” said another article.
But it’s not just about the hardware. Ternus has put the iPhone at the center of his “intelligent personal assistant” strategy, a vision that could define the company for years to come. Steve Jobs did something similar in 2001 with the Mac, less than 10 months before he announced the iPod.
At the time, many observers thought the PC’s days were numbered. At a Macworld New York keynote, Jobs called out bearish quotes from industry wonks like Walt Mossberg and the leaders of Compaq and Gateway.
“This is what everyone else is telling us. That our PC is waning if not the hole being dug,” Jobs said at the time, pointing at a tombstone for the “Beloved PC” on the screen behind him. “We don’t think the PC is dying at all. We don’t think the PC is moving away from the center at all. We think it’s evolving, just like it has since it was invented.”
“We think the PC is on the threshold of entering its third great age,” Jobs added, a prediction driven by the proliferation of digital devices at the time, including camcorders, digital cameras, and DVD players.
The Mac would form the center of a “digital hub” that would connect these disparate devices and, in Jobs’ words, “add value” to all of them.
Later that year, Jobs pulled the iPod out of his pocket, a device seemingly developed to answer the question, “Why do you still need a PC?” The device turned out to be an enormous hit, driving Apple’s profits quarter after quarter and ultimately helping lead to the development of the iPhone.
Today, with the iPhone on the cusp of its 20th anniversary, Ternus is facing a version of the same question Jobs took on in 2001. We don’t know if Ternus is quietly sitting on an iPod-like product, one that will secure the iPhone’s position as Apple’s hub for years to come. But he is firmly rebutting the idea that the iPhone is past its prime.
“If you were designing the ideal version of this hub from scratch, how would you do it?” Ternus asked before listing the ingredients: a powerful processor, high-resolution cameras, persistent networking, and on-device AI.
It helps that the iPhone is one of the most powerful personal computing devices around, giving it an edge in the compute-hungry AI era. Its portability and adaptability make it, for many people, the only computing device they need. Even among those who own laptops and iPads, the iPhone is often the one device they can’t live without. Plenty of people leave home without their laptops. Almost no one leaves without their phones.
That combination of power and portability has given Apple a privileged position in the AI world. Other companies have attempted to unseat the iPhone with all manner of wearable devices, but none have succeeded.
Instead of sidelining the iPhone in favor of the next flashy thing, Ternus is leaning into it instead. In a way, he’s bringing Apple around to what the rest of us already know: The iPhone is pretty great, and maybe we don’t need to replace it with something else. Yet.

articles.title: 10 Self-help books for people navigating life with ADHD
articles.text:
10 Self-help books for people navigating life with ADHD
Discover 10 insightful self-help books for ADHD that offer practical strategies for focus, productivity, emotional balance, and daily success.
Living with ADHD can feel like having dozens of browser tabs open at once. You may be full of energy and ideas one moment, then struggle to focus the next. While ADHD can bring creativity, curiosity, and spontaneity, it can also make organisation, time management, and emotional regulation harder.
The good news is that countless authors, psychologists, and ADHD experts have developed practical tools to help people better understand how their brains work.
The best ADHD books don't promise to "fix" anyone. Instead, they provide strategies that work with the ADHD brain rather than against it. Whether you're newly diagnosed or have been managing ADHD for years, these books offer valuable insights that can help you thrive.
10 Self-help books for people navigating life with ADHD
1. Driven to Distraction by Edward M. Hallowell and John J. Ratey
Considered a classic in ADHD literature, this book helped bring widespread attention to the condition. The authors explain ADHD through real-life stories and practical examples, helping readers recognise patterns in their own lives.
The book explores common challenges such as impulsivity, distractibility, and difficulty with organisation while also highlighting the strengths often associated with ADHD. Its compassionate approach makes it an excellent starting point for anyone seeking to better understand themselves.
2. ADHD 2.0 by Edward M. Hallowell and John J. Ratey
Written decades after Driven to Distraction, this updated guide incorporates newer research and modern strategies for managing ADHD.
The authors discuss how brain science has evolved and provide practical advice for improving focus, building routines, and leveraging ADHD-related strengths. The book is concise, accessible, and filled with actionable suggestions that readers can apply immediately.
3. Taking Charge of Adult ADHD by Russell A. Barkley
Russell Barkley is one of the world's leading ADHD researchers, and this book serves as a practical guide for adults managing the condition.
It focuses on evidence-based techniques for improving organisation, reducing procrastination, and developing effective daily systems. Readers appreciate its straightforward advice and realistic solutions for common ADHD struggles.
4. Your Brain's Not Broken by Tamara Rosier
Many people with ADHD spend years feeling frustrated by productivity methods that seem to work for everyone else. Tamara Rosier explains why traditional approaches often fail and offers strategies tailored specifically to ADHD minds.
The book emphasises self-understanding, practical planning, and creating systems that align with the way ADHD brains naturally function.
5. The ADHD Advantage by Dale Archer
Rather than focusing solely on challenges, this book explores the unique strengths that often accompany ADHD.
Dale Archer argues that many successful entrepreneurs, innovators, and creative thinkers share ADHD traits. The book encourages readers to recognise their abilities and learn how to channel them effectively in both personal and professional settings.
6. Order from Chaos by Jaclyn Paul
Organisation can be one of the biggest hurdles for people with ADHD. This book provides practical systems for managing schedules, tasks, and responsibilities without relying on rigid productivity methods.
Jaclyn Paul offers realistic solutions that acknowledge the realities of ADHD while helping readers create structure in their daily lives.
7. Fast Minds by Craig Surman and Tim Bilkey
This book combines scientific research with practical exercises designed to improve attention, memory, and productivity.
The authors focus on helping readers identify specific ADHD-related challenges and develop personalised strategies for overcoming them. Its workbook-style approach makes it particularly useful for those who learn best through action.
8. The Smart but Scattered Guide to Success by Peg Dawson and Richard Guare
Many individuals with ADHD struggle with executive functioning skills such as planning, prioritising, and follow-through.
This book breaks those skills into manageable steps and provides exercises for strengthening them over time. It is especially valuable for students, young professionals, and anyone seeking better organisational habits.
9. Delivered from Distraction by Edward M. Hallowell and John J. Ratey
Serving as a follow-up to Driven to Distraction, this book offers updated advice and deeper insights into living successfully with ADHD.
It includes practical guidance for relationships, work, education, and personal growth while emphasising that ADHD does not have to define a person's limitations.
10. Thriving with Adult ADHD by Phil Boissiere
This approachable guide focuses on helping adults create sustainable habits and routines.
The book addresses common issues such as procrastination, overwhelm, emotional regulation, and productivity. Its step-by-step strategies make it particularly useful for readers looking for practical changes they can implement right away.
Why these books matter
ADHD is about more than attention. It can affect planning, emotions, motivation, memory, and everyday life. The right book can offer practical strategies and reassurance that these challenges are shared by many.
These ten books combine science, personal experiences, and practical advice, showing that managing ADHD is not about changing who you are, but understanding how your mind works and using its strengths.

articles.title: OpenAI claims 10,000 of its AI agents solved one of mathematics' hardest problems in 88 hours
articles.text:
Crystal ball: OpenAI has released a paper claiming that an unreleased AI model solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the Clay Mathematics Institute's Millennium Prize Problems. The company said the system reached its result in 88 hours by coordinating as many as 10,000 AI agents and producing a formal proof in Lean.
Mathematicians outside the company will now review the paper. If the proof holds up, it could show that AI systems can help solve some of mathematics' hardest open problems, rather than simply produce convincing-looking answers.
The Navier-Stokes equations describe how fluids move. They are used in weather forecasting, aerodynamics, and other areas of fluid mechanics. The Millennium problem asks whether the equations always yield smooth solutions in three dimensions or whether, under certain conditions, they can develop a singularity – a point at which the mathematical model breaks down.
OpenAI said its proof identifies such a breakdown. The result does not mean water or air will behave in physically impossible ways. It concerns the limits of the equations as a mathematical system, not a prediction that fluids will suddenly violate the laws of physics.
The Clay Mathematics Institute selected the Navier-Stokes question as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems in 2000. Each carries a $1 million prize, and only one, the Poincaré conjecture, has previously been solved.
OpenAI's work depended on a multi-agent setup rather than a single model attempting the problem alone. The company said groups of AI agents pursued different lines of reasoning while OpenAI researchers passed useful ideas among them. Researcher Dan Roberts described the process as "a bumblebee cross-pollinating across different groups and delivering different bits of information."
The agents used Lean, a formal proof language that checks whether every logical step follows the system's rules. Lean does not determine whether a result is important, but it can establish whether the steps in a proof are valid under a defined set of assumptions. That makes it useful for AI-generated mathematics, where a model can produce convincing but flawed reasoning in ordinary text.
The project reflects a growing effort to train models on tasks with hard pass-fail signals. In mathematics, a proof can be tested. In code, a program can be run. That gives reinforcement-learning systems a way to learn through repeated attempts, errors, and corrections. The same approach is harder to apply in areas where correctness is less clear-cut, including creative work and ethical questions.
OpenAI and other AI companies have reported progress on open mathematical problems over the past year. In January, OpenAI and Harmonic said their systems had solved an Erdős problem. Some mathematicians said the result resembled earlier human work and questioned whether the systems had produced a genuinely new approach.
The Navier-Stokes claim is more consequential because of the problem's prominence and difficulty. OpenAI said it turned its attention to the problem after learning that other researchers were pursuing related work. The company said it "did not see any of their work through any means."
The announcement came shortly after Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematics professor at New York University, said he had been investigating related questions with a mathematician who works at Anthropic, an OpenAI competitor.
The compute required for OpenAI's effort was substantial. The company said it ran up to 10,000 agents, a process that likely required millions of dollars in computing resources. OpenAI research scientist Noam Brown called it "a very expensive process," but said costs should fall as the company improves its systems and infrastructure.
For many mathematicians, the issue is larger than whether the proof holds up. Terence Tao, a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, has warned that AI could weaken the discipline if machines begin solving major problems with limited human involvement. "The effort needed to solve problems is often very instructive," he told The New York Times.

articles.title: Microsoft reportedly gives secret Xbox Game Pass discounts to churned subscribers to reel them back in — targeted offers slash up to 30% off the regular price
articles.text:
Microsoft reportedly gives secret Xbox Game Pass discounts to churned subscribers to reel them back in — targeted offers slash up to 30% off the regular price
If you play hard to get, you could get Xbox Game Pass for cheaper; at least that is what numerous users are reporting on a Reddit thread. One Xbox Game Pass subscriber shared a screenshot of Microsoft offering them the Ultimate plan for $16.09 for a month, 30% lower than the standard $22.99. Their secret? Cancel Xbox Game Pass almost every month.
Dynamic win-back discounts are perhaps the oldest trick in the book, but they remain widely used because of their effectiveness in re-engaging customers who have stopped buying a product or, in Microsoft's case, canceled their Xbox Game Pass subscription. These targeted offers, often disguised as "We Miss You" or "Welcome back" deals, aim to win back lost customers with exclusive or time-limited discounts.
According to the Redditor, they have used Xbox Game Pass on and off for about two years. However, instead of committing to an annual plan, the user frequently paused and resubscribed. In the Redditor's words, they were "not doing any sort of tricks lol...just got the offer randomly because I cancel gamepass almost every month, so maybe this was their way of keeping me."
This kind of customer behavior is not uncommon among subscription services, since buyers seek to maximize value and avoid unnecessary spending. Apparently, Microsoft seemingly noticed this user and proactively offered a 30% discount, dropping the Xbox Game Pass Ultimate price from $22.99 to $16.09 for a year. And it worked. The Redditor confirmed that they took the offer and locked in for the entire year.
At least one other Redditor confirmed they also received the same $16.09 offer. The thread quickly filled with additional posts as users shared their experiences with Xbox Game Pass discounts. For example, one Reddit user said that when they logged in with a secondary account on their Xbox console, they saw an $18 offer for 12 months of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate. Their main account allegedly never receives offers like this. Meanwhile, other users chimed in to report receiving $ 20-per-month offers.
It is unclear what criteria Microsoft uses to distribute these win-back discounts. Many speculate that the company may be considering activity, subscription history, or even multiple accounts. The discounts do not seem limited to the U.S., where the Redditor lives. Users in the thread have reported similar discounts in regions like México.
Despite Microsoft slashing Xbox Game Pass pricing earlier this year, many gamers still resort to digital key marketplaces such as Eneba, G2A, or Loaded, where one month of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate can cost as little as $9.28. By running targeted annual promotions, Microsoft can encourage subscribers to stick with Xbox Game Pass, secure long-term revenue, and avoid the risks of month-to-month cancellation.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
However, these targeted discounts raise an important question: should Microsoft not reward loyal Xbox Game Pass subscribers with similar exclusive discounts? Win-back promotions are great for bringing back former subscribers, but long-time users will feel overlooked and see no reason to commit, since the generous deals go to those who cancel and return.
