articles.title: SA’s Injini launches AI for Education venture builder, incubation programme - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
The Cape Town-based Injini, an ed-tech incubator, accelerator and think tank, has launched its AI for Education venture builder and incubation programme, which takes pre-formed teams from the ideation stage to launching market-ready, impactful ed-tech startups.
Founded in 2017, Injini, which is a member of the UVU Africa Group, is a registered non-profit company that exists for the sole purpose of improving educational outcomes in Sub-Saharan Africa. Its programmes and research via the Injini Think Tank contribute towards its mission to increase the quality, accessibility, and relevance of education in the region. It announced its latest cohort earlier this year.
Injini has now launched its AI for Education venture builder and incubation programme, supported by philanthropic funder Coefficient Giving. The eight-month initiative, which will support 12 pre-formed teams, has a simple goal – to test AI tools that work in African classrooms, then back the most promising with funding and support to grow.
Phase one, which lasts for five months, is the Venture Build phase, where the teams will move month-by-month from problem validation and customer research through solution design, building a functional AI-powered MVP, and executing a live pilot to generate real-world usage and value data. Phase two is the Incubation phase, which lasts for three months, and will see the top five teams work on developing a market-ready product, strengthening their business model canvas, building a go-to-market strategy, and receiving MEL support.
These five ventures also receive equity-free seed capital of $25,000 each to continue their journey.
“We’ve spent years engaging with brilliant people across the region who understand education problems intimately, but lack the team, capital, or clear path to build a solution,” said Krista Davidson, executive director at Injini.
“Add to this that Africa is significantly underrepresented in the data training AI tools. If we don’t build our own solutions now, we risk ed-tech that simply doesn’t work for African classrooms. This venture builder is aimed at closing these gaps.”
Applications are open to small teams, with three or more co-founders preferred. All team members must be based in South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Zambia, or Zimbabwe. Applications are open here until September 27.

articles.title: New German AI research lab Grubel raises €3 million to build systems that adapt to individual legal cases | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Grubel, a Munich- and Tübingen-based AI research lab developing systems that adapt to individual legal matters, has raised €3 million in pre-Seed funding to support research, product development, and team expansion.
The round was led by venture capital firm Point Nine, with participation from angel investors including Jeff Dean (Google’s former chief scientist), Chris Ré (Stanford professor and Together AI co-founder), Ion Stoica (UC Berkeley Professor and Databricks co-founder), and Harvey co-founders Gabe Pereyra and Winston Weinberg, among others.
“Complex legal matters do not come with ready-made training data, task environments, or clear tests of success. We are automating the AI specialisation loop that identifies the right information, curates it into training data and environments, adapts the system to the matter, and tests whether its work meets the required standard,” said Reinhard Heckel, co-founder of Grubel.
Founded in 2026 by machine-learning researchers Moritz Hardt and Heckel, Grubel is automating AI specialisation: gathering and preparing relevant information, adapting the system to the legal work at hand, and testing whether its work meets the required standards.
Hardt is a director at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and a former UC Berkeley professor and Google Brain researcher. He has co-developed test-time training and co-authored Lawma. Heckel is a TUM professor of machine learning, currently on leave and formerly a researcher at IBM Research. He focuses on data-centric machine learning and helped create DataComp-LM and OpenThoughts.
According to the company, complex knowledge work beyond coding remains surprisingly dependent on highly skilled human labour, with AI still playing only a limited role. Grubel opines that this gap is particularly apparent in legal services.
The company notes that legal AI has lagged in part because complex legal work is both highly specialised and very difficult to evaluate. It often requires expertise specific to an individual matter, including its facts, documents, terminology, prior work product, and client standards.
It further notes that today, teams of engineers and lawyers build specialised AI systems for specific legal workflows by curating data, adapting the systems, and evaluating their performance. Although this specialisation is powerful, it requires substantial manual effort. It states that an engineering team cannot build and maintain a separate system for every legal matter.
Grubel claims to be automating that specialisation process. Its thesis is that every matter needs its own AI. To make that possible, the company is automating the process of specialising an AI system for each matter. Its specialisation loop has three components: a data engine that discovers and curates task-relevant data for each matter or client; a test-time adaptation layer that adapts both the model and the agent to the matter before acting; and a continual evaluation framework that checks the work against standards derived from the matter itself. The loop repeats until the system delivers what the legal task demands.
It’s bringing data curation, adaptation, and evaluation into a specialisation loop that trains and improves on the matter itself.
“Over the past two to three years, we’ve seen many legal AI companies emerge, but few are pushing the boundaries of AI research in the legal field as ambitiously as Reinhard, Moritz and the Grubel team. We believe their approach can unlock new capabilities in legal AI and, over time, other forms of complex knowledge work. We’re excited to support them on this journey,” said Louis Coppey, Partner at Point Nine.
The company plans to use this capital to support its research, product development, and team expansion. An initial evaluation showed that Grubel’s specialisation loop can improve performance over general-purpose frontier systems on the legal tasks tested. The company aims to further develop its automated specialisation loop to improve performance on complex legal work while allowing more routine tasks to be handled by smaller, more efficient models.

articles.title: Nintendo unveils The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 for $520 — First-ever special-edition Switch 2 drops October 19, alongside $100 Pro Controller, pre-orders live
articles.text:
Nintendo unveils The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 for $520 — First-ever special-edition Switch 2 drops October 19, alongside $100 Pro Controller, pre-orders live
No, this is not an Ocarina of Time-themed Switch 2.
Nintendo just aired one of the most important Directs of the Switch 2 generation, showcasing the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake in all its glory. The presentation also brought along the announcement of the first special edition Switch 2 hardware: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition. The console costs $519.99, but there's also an identically themed Pro Controller for $99.99 that you can pre-order right now — either item ships later this year on October 29.
- Pre-order The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Switch 2
- Pre-order The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Pro Controller
- Pre-order The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Carrying Case
The company's first handheld to be adorned in special edition Zelda makeup was the Game Boy Advance SP released in 2004 alongside The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap. The first home console to receive the same treatment was The Wind Waker HD edition of the Wii U in 2013. Most recently, we got a Tears of the Kingdom-themed Switch OLED in 2023, followed by the Hyrule Edition of the Switch Lite next year.
Across every handled and home console released, The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary special edition Switch 2 will be the 12th piece of Zelda-themed hardware Nintendo has put out. Moreover, it took the original Switch just a few months to get its first limited-edition hardware (Monster Hunter XX Special Pack), but the Switch 2 has clearly taken its time with this design, and it's sure to be a collector's item.
The tablet itself is mostly the same boring black except for a few golden triangles at the back. However, the Joy-Cons feature a beautiful green design with a Tri-Force symbol on the left. The dock is a gorgeous, two-tone golden and black color with a very bold Tri-Force theme across the front and some easter eggs on the back. Even the packaging is supposed to have textured foil cover art. The console will retail for $520 and does not come with any game.
Alongside the console, there's a Switch 2 Pro Controller that looks very similar to the Joy-Cons, with a green and gold theme that combines elements of the Triforce with a crest emblem. It comes as is for $100, but you can also get it with a subtly themed display stand for $110. Finally, there's also a $40 carrying case adorned with Zelda illustrations. You even get a custom, green-colored microfiber cloth inside and a screen protector.
Keep in mind that all of this hardware celebrates the 40th anniversary of the Zelda franchise, which already passed earlier this year. It has nothing to do with the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake and, as such, the game is not included in the $520 limited edition Switch 2. Pre-orders for all the items discussed above are open, and they will be released on October 29, 2026. The Ocarina of Time remake drops next month, on November 19, 2026, and will be sold separately for $60.

articles.title: Apple Watch’s new feature listens to your chats and recaps them | TechCrunch
articles.text:
At its Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, Apple launched a meeting notetaker for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, one of a series of new audio intelligence features that can listen to sounds through your Apple Watch.
The feature, called Siri Recap, uses ambient listening to take high-level notes of your conversations, according to the company. Apple Intelligence will automatically generate a title, summary, and key points from the conversation, which can then be reviewed in the Siri app.
Apple said that you can choose to keep this feature always on, set up a schedule, or turn off completely.
The notetaker wasn’t the only audio-focused feature introduced for the Watch during the event. Apple’s new audio intelligence features also include Shazam, which can identify songs instantly. This means Apple has finally caught up to Google’s Now Playing feature. The Watch can recognize loud sounds like sirens, alarms, doorbells, or a baby crying and notify users.
Apple also introduced a feature called Live Rewind, which lets users recap 15 seconds of conversation when they double-press the Digital Crown.
Apple emphasized that the features don’t store recordings and that raw audio is inaccessible. The Siri Recap feature doesn’t identify speakers either. Users can access Live Rewind recaps, which are end-to-end encrypted. Despite these guardrails, an always-listening feature will likely raise privacy concerns because Siri Recap may still capture sensitive information in its summaries.
Besides some of the privacy features, Siri Recap sounds similar to other notetakers like Granola and Circleback, which also have Apple Watch apps.

articles.title: GTA 6 PS5 controller pre-orders live — build-up ahead of two new DualSense pads dropping tomorrow
articles.text:
Live
The giant of a video game release is nearly upon us, and Sony is getting well and truly involved with GTA 6 PS5 controllers beginning tomorrow on two very cool looking DualSense variations.
Two new limited-edition GTA 6 PS5 controllers are up for grabs tomorrow: one black, one white. Both share a lot of the same design sensibilities and features, but I think both look slick as heck. They are both unmistakably 'Vice City' with palm tree emblems and fronds draped over the pad, while the glints of pink shine wonderfully through on the white or black backgrounds, and the shimmering finish on both does a great job of evoking neon lights.
Both DualSense controllers will cost you $84.99 / £74.99 and will release alongside GTA 6 on November 19. However, there will be a slight variation in availability. The white GTA 6 DualSense will be "available in limited quantities globally at direct.playstation.com and at participating retailers", says Sony. The black GTA 6 DualSense will be "available in limited quantities exclusively through direct.playstation.com where available" — so that means in the UK and US.
We expect the usual suspects to get involved in pre-order listings on both sides of the Atlantic, and we will be casting our eager eye over those, and a wider net more generally, to make sure we get you the best links and info as soon as we see them. We're starting today to get our flag in the ground early, so you know where to be in the run-up to stock dropping.
US GTA 6 DualSense pre-orders – quick links
- 🅿️GTA 6 Black Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at PS Direct (exclusive to PS Direct)🅿️
- 🅿️GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at PS Direct🅿️
- 📦GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Amazon📦
- 🔆GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Walmart🔆
- 🏷️GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Best Buy🏷️
- 🎯GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Target🎯
- 🎮GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at GameStop🎮
UK GTA 6 DualSense pre-orders – quick links
- 🅿️GTA 6 Black Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at PS Direct (exclusive to PS Direct)🅿️
- 🅿️GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at PS Direct🅿️
- 📦GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Amazon UK📦
- ©️GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Currys©️
- 📱GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at EE📱
- 🧸GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Smyths Toys🧸
- 𝓥 GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Very 𝓥
- 🟥GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at Argos🟥
- 🟡GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at ShopTo🟡
- 🎮GTA 6 White Limited Edition DualSense: Check for stock at The Game Collection🎮
Should you pre-order a GTA 6 Limited Edition PS5 controller?
This is perhaps an even easier recommendation to make than the one I did before the game was available to pre-order: in short, you should absolutely, 100%, definitely consider placing a pre-order on these GTA 6 DualSense controllers if you can, rather than waiting and hoping they remain available in the long run.
These are accessories — that will be available in "limited quantities", according to Sony — that will coincide with the release of the biggest thing in all of entertainment ever. As a result, the demand will likely be the highest on DualSense controller editions we've ever seen — and perhaps on any accessory ever.
Yes, there are two different editions which will hopefully spread the load of the demand, but I think placing a pre-order if you can is by far the safest option if you're at all interested in one of these PS5 controllers.
GTA 6 Limited Edition PS5 controllers: cut to the chase
- Price: $84.99 / £74.99
- Pre-order date: September 10, 2026; 10am ET / 10am local time in Europe
- Release date: November 19, 2026
- Design: Sony describes the limited edition DualSense controllers as pads that "each capture the essence of Vice City, from bright days along the coast to vibrant city nights. Both editions feature a shimmering, color-shifting finish that brings together the hues of a Vice City sunset and the glow of neon lights. They both also feature custom palm tree details molded directly into the controller, adding a unique tactile element alongside official Grand Theft Auto VI branding." There's no denying they do look pretty slick.
I've covered almost every PS5-related hardware and limited edition release, pre-order, or launch since the Sony console first came out in 2020. I've helped thousands of folks get their hands on things like the PlayStation Portal, 30th Anniversary hardware, and loads more. As a result, I'm battle-hardened and a grizzled veteran when it comes to covering launches and ensuring you have all the right info and links to get the item you want. I'm also a huge PlayStation head and a small-to-medium-time collector of PS5 hardware, so I'm definitely going to be interested in bagging one or both of these controllers myself — something you can count on from all of us who man this live page as pre-orders roll out.
LIVE: Latest Updates
Remember, the DualSense is compatible with PC as well
PC players will sadly have to wait a little while longer for GTA 6 to release on that platform, but that doesn't mean you have to miss out on the hype. The DualSense controller is fully compatible with PC via USB and Bluetooth, so if you feel like you want to be involved with the release in some way, one of these controllers is an option for you. Maybe you can play through GTA 5 with it and pretend it's the new game instead!
What about a special edition console for GTA 6?
I am somewhat surprised that Rockstar hasn't pushed things even further by launching a limited-edition PS5 or Xbox console to coincide with the launch of GTA 6. It feels like the natural thing to do.
We may all be in for a big surprise at some point over the next couple of months if one does surface, but it feels quite late for it to happen now. Instead, I'm sure there will be a few console bundles available with the game (and maybe featuring these controllers) when the launch comes around for folks buying hardware just for GTA 6.
What are the chances of a restock if you miss out?
Given the expected popularity of GTA 6 and these DualSense controllers, I feel like it's almost guaranteed that they will sell out in this first drop. That popularity, however, means that further restocks are very likely in the run-up (and after) launch.
Sony has been fairly regular when it comes to restocking other limited-edition controllers, and I don't think it will be any different with the GTA 6 models. Just be aware that the Black version is a PS Direct exclusive, so that one will be harder to get — even if there's a restock.
When does Amazon drop the GTA 6 controllers?
As one of the biggest and most popular places to shop online, there's always a lot of interest in when Amazon will make these controllers available to buy. Given its dominance, though, it rarely follows the expected plan announced by Sony.
Sure, it could follow suit and go live at 10am local time with everyone else, given it's such a significant launch, but the more likely scenario is that it just ignores everything and puts the controllers up whenever it feels like later in the day. It might even wait until tomorrow.
Because of that, it'll be one we'll be checking and refreshing regularly so that you don't miss the drop.
Where is stock likely to drop first?
Retailers are supposed to stick to the 10am local time embargo before launching preorders for these DualSense controllers, but as we've seen with previous drops, some decide to be a little cheeky and kick things off early.
The Wolverine controllers, for example, were available at both Target in the US and Currys in the UK a short time ahead of the announced launch time. We'll be watching both of them closely once again to see if they repeat themselves for this launch.
Given it's GTA 6, though, things might be a bit stricter this time when it comes to putting the controllers up for sale, so any early drops aren't guaranteed.
Return of the Mack...
Mack is back! As TechRadar's deals editor, I'll be taking over from Rob to post all the latest updates on the GTA 6 PS5 controller preorders.
I'm off for now - but we're still going
I'm passing the steering of our GTA 6 PS5 controller pre-order ship to one of my excellent colleagues now, as I step away for the evening (and to prepare for a trip to BlizzCon too!).
Keep it right here for the best information and links in preparation for tomorrow's pre-orders kicking off!
Even the packaging looks dope — if it's real
Our friends at GamesRadar+ have spotted a social media post that shows an image of the packaging — and even that looks slick as heck! If it's real, of course...
Which retailers are the ones to go for first?
If I'm understanding the PS Blog post correctly — and I think I am, I've done loads of these launches now, though Sony can be ambiguous — then I reckon you're best first port of call is going top be PlayStation Direct. And that's on both sides of the Atlantic.
US retailers have been pretty good on the last limited edition releases and all of Walmart, Amazon, Best Buy, Target, and GameStop have reliably followed with stock. We'd still err toward the former three though for the best and likely-quickest shopping experience.
In the UK, things have been a bit different in recent times. Amazon UK has been very unreliable when it comes to limited edition PS5 hardware or accessory stock. For example, it still hasn't got Marvel's Wolverine DualSense stock. However, the likes of Smyths Toys, Currys,. and Very have all been reliable with the last release or two.
An early bit of advice to be in position, well, early
It sounds obvious, being ready early, but actually what I mean more specifically is that last time out with the Marvel's Wolverine PS5 collection of controllers and console covers, retailers in the UK, particularly, actually went live comfortably earlier than the 10am start time.
So much so, in fact,m that PS Direct itself also pulled the trigger before 10am in the end; such were the options available to customers before the official start time.
As a result, it'll definitely pay to be as ready to go as you possibly can earlier than 10am ET or 10am local time — perhaps aim for 9.30am and get poised.
So: which one do you like the look of most?
As I said, I think the Black one just pips it for me in terms of my aesthetic tastes, but which one are you most likely to pre-order? Let me know in the poll below!
...and more than just a pattern
And I also really like the look of the properly moulded and formed palm tree fronds that are raised off the surface of the DualSense.
A lot of previous designs haven't altered the physical feel of the PS5 controller that much, so I really like this change and feature of this particular limited edition design.
The details are fabulous...
I really like the flashy details of the glinty art style in both the black and white variants, and this close up of the white model really shows how the glimmering and shimmering speckles will change in the light too. Nice.
When and where are the GTA 6 PS5 controller pre-orders?
OK, the first part of this is easy: GTA 6 PS5 controller pre-orders kick off at 10am ET in the US, and 10am local time everywhere else. Boom.
The second part, availability, is a little more complex, but only in the sense of the difference between the two variants. If my parsing of the PS Blog post is correct, it appears that the Black GTA 6 DualSense will be exclusive to PS Direct, while the white variant will be the one that's available at both PS Direct and other retailers.
What, and how much, are the GTA 6 PS5 controller pre-orders?
In terms of what, there will be two distinct GTA 6 PS5 controllers up for pre-order tomorrow.
Sony is attractively naming them, officially, as 'DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI Black Limited Edition' and 'DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI White Limited Edition'. The black and white overarching colorway is indeed the biggest thing that separates them, but they both look slick as heck in my view.
There's that shimmering blue look on both, palm tree fronds and forms draped over the pads, and pink accents that punch through the black or white really pleasingly. I think I prefer the Black one, but it's a close run thing.
There's no difference in price, though, and both will cost you $84.99 / £74.99 — the standard price for DualSenses right now.
These are going to be hot stuff...
Not only are these two controllers absolute beauties — at least, I think — they are tied to the biggest entertainment release in history.
As a result, I predict the demand for these is going to be huge; absolutely wild, in fact. I know that recent Limited Edition PS5 controllers haven't sold out like some, but surely the safe bet here is that stock will fly.
Because of that I reckon it'll pay to get in position early with bookmarking the above links, getting account information in order, and making sure you're fully informed ahead of stock dropping. tomorrow.

articles.title: Apple irrumpe en el mercado de plegables con el iPhone Duo: la pesadilla de Samsung y Xiaomi se ha vuelto realidad
articles.text:
Después de tantísimos rumores y especulaciones, Apple se ha animado a probar un nuevo factor de forma en su catálogo de móviles. Que iPhone Fold, que iPhone Ultra, el primer plegable de la manzana finalmente llega al mercado con un nombre que la compañía logró mantener en secreto casi hasta último momento: iPhone Duo.
Tras meses de hype, el iPhone Duo es una realidad y pretende ser la pesadilla que tanto han temido rivales como Samsung y Xiaomi. Apple llega tarde a la fiesta, es cierto, pero irrumpe en el mercado de la forma que mejor sabe hacerlo: a lo Apple. Y esto queda en evidencia tanto en el apartado de diseño como en el de funcionalidades.
El iPhone Duo seguramente comparte virtudes y defectos con otros plegables ya disponibles en el mercado. Pero es un iPhone, y por sí solo eso tiene el peso suficiente para cambiar el curso de ciertos mercados. En Estados Unidos, donde los smartphones de Apple acaparan casi la totalidad de la atención del público, puede dar un vuelco total al modo en que este mira a los foldables.
Apple afirma que el iPhone Duo es el móvil más delgado de la compañía, gracias al acomodamiento de componentes en el espacio ocupado por el módulo de la cámara. Además, el chasis se ha fabricado en titanio para mejorar la durabilidad. Y presume el mérito de ser el primer iPhone de la historia compatible con el Apple Pencil, aunque tal vez no desde su lanzamiento.
Los de la manzana mencionan que el iPhone Duo se podrá usar con el Apple Pencil con USB-C para tomar notas, dibujar y más. Sin embargo, indican que esta capacidad se añadirá "más adelante" este año, lo que da a pensar que se producirá hacia finales de 2026.
El iPhone Duo saca provecho de su diseño tipo pasaporte y de la fluidez de iOS 27
La pantalla interior es de 7,6 pulgadas, lo que la convierte en el panel más grande jamás incorporado en un iPhone hasta la fecha. En el caso de la pantalla exterior, se trata de un panel de 5,4 pulgadas. El diseño tipo pasaporte permite controlarlo fácilmente con una mano cuando está cerrado y brinda fácil acceso a toda la interfaz al estar abierto.
Buena parte de la experiencia con el iPhone Duo depende del software. Aquí es donde entra en juego una versión optimizada de iOS 27, que destaca por tener el dock ubicado de forma vertical contra el borde derecho de la pantalla. Lo último aplica tanto para el panel exterior como el interior.
Apple le ha dado al iPhone Duo un enfoque basado en la productividad gracias a la posibilidad de ejecutar dos aplicaciones lado a lado cuando está desplegado a tamaño completo. El smartphone también se puede usar semiplegado e incluso tiene un modo standby mejorado. Y como no podía ser de otra manera, la compañía ofrece a los desarrolladores una forma fácil de adaptar sus apps al factor de forma.
La ingeniería detrás del primer iPhone plegable
En cuanto a la pantalla interior, Apple menciona que el iPhone Duo incorpora una capa nanotexturizada que disminuye la visibilidad de la marca del pliegue y que ayuda a que el panel se vea plano. Asimismo, se encarga de reducir los reflejos y resplandores.
Otro detalle interesante del iPhone Duo es que Apple finalmente lo ha dotado de una cámara bajo la pantalla interior. Aquí la compañía ha implementado una solución bastante curiosa que permite descubrir la cámara cuando sea necesario, ocultándola detrás de los píxeles cuando no se la necesita. Vale aclarar, no obstante, que los californianos no han revelado la calidad de este sensor, al que se refieren oficialmente solo como "cámara FaceTime bajo la pantalla".
En lo que corresponde a los componentes internos, los de la manzana han implementado un diseño de múltiples capas que también sirve para mantener la pantalla flexible lo más plana posible, sin que su integridad se degrade con los pliegues continuos. Para ello, también dependen del uso de placas internas de fibra de carbono
En cuanto a las cámaras traseras, el iPhone Duo incorpora un sensor principal Fusión de 48 megapíxeles, acompañado de un teleleobjetivo 2x de 12 MP. La cámara frontal, en tanto, es de 12 MP. El uso de las cámaras está optimizado para videollamadas en FaceTime y, tal y como sucede en otros plegables, se puede compartir lo que ve la cámara en la pantalla exterior para facilitar la creación de contenido.
El iPhone Duo llega equipado con el potente chip A20 Pro que se anunció con los nuevos iPhone 18 Pro y Pro Max. El mismo se basa en un proceso litográfico de 2 nanómetros y cuenta con un nuevo empaquetado inspirado en el de los SoC de la serie M de Apple Silicon. La CPU cuenta con 6 núcleos, dos de los cuales Apple llama "supernúcleos", que brindan rendimiento de escritorio, mientras que la GPU mejorada es de 7 núcleos. Por otra parte, el plegable integra un módem C2 de desarrollo propio.
Otro punto en común entre el iPhone Duo y otros plegables es que la batería está dividida en dos partes. Si bien Apple no ha mencionado la capacidad de la misma, cosa que no sorprende porque no acostumbra hacerlo, sí ha prometido que ofrecerá energía suficiente para durar todo el día.
En cuanto a otras características rumoreadas que finalmente se han confirmado, hay que mencionar el regreso de Touch ID como método de autenticación biométrica. El iPhone Duo no tiene Face ID, pero los de Cupertino prometen compensarlo ofreciendo la opción de vincular más de una huella dactilar.
Lo que sí ha sorprendido es que el iPhone Duo finalmente tiene certificación IP68. Esto significa que está protegido contra el polvo y el agua al mismo nivel que muchos móviles de formato convencional. De esta manera, el plegable se suma a los Pixel 10 Pro Fold y Pixel 11 Pro Fold, que fueron los primeros plegables en obtenerla.
Disponibilidad y precios del iPhone Duo: prepárate para el sablazo
Mark Gurman acertó con sus filtraciones del iPhone Duo. El móvil se lanzará en Estados Unidos con un precio inicial de 1.999 dólares por la versión de entrada de 256 GB de almacenamiento. También habrá disponibles modelos con 512 GB, 1 TB y 2 TB de espacio interno; este último costará ni más ni menos que 3.199 dólares.
¿Y qué pasa en España? El iPhone Duo estará disponible desde el primer día. Esto destierra los rumores de que el estreno del dispositivo se daría únicamente en Estados Unidos. Pero prepara la cartera porque tendrás que desembolsar bastante para obtener el primer plegable de Apple.
El iPhone Duo de 256 GB se venderá a cambio de 2.339 euros. La versión de 512 GB costará 2.589 euros y la de 1 TB se conseguirá por 3.089 euros. Si te sientes particularmente atrevido, también puedes optar por la variante de 2 TB, siempre y cuando estés dispuesto a desembolsar 3.839 euros.
Apple ofrecerá el iPhone Duo en dos colores: blanco estelar y cielo nocturno. Las reservas se iniciarán recién el 16 de octubre a partir de las 05:00, hora del Pacífico; es decir, las 14:00 de España. Las entregas, por su parte, comenzarán el 23 de octubre.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (September 9, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (September 9, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
From QNu Labs’ Rs 200-crore raise and leadership changes at Snap to payments moves by Jio Payment Solutions and Pluxee, YourStory brings you today's headlines and the latest news across sectors.
Featured stories
QNu Labs raises Rs 200 crore in Series A1 round
Quantum cybersecurity startup QNu Labs raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest, with Sony Innovation Fund, Gaja Capital and Artha Ventures participating. The company will expand R&D and go-to-market in India and overseas.
Snap’s Ajit Mohan steps down as chief business officer
Ajit Mohan has stepped down as Snap’s Chief Business Officer and will return to Singapore to spend more time with his family. Snap has named EMEA President Ronan Harris as Chief Commercial Officer as part of the leadership changes.
Jacob Coxon warns labs of reckless superintelligence race
Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has resigned after three years in pretraining roles across OpenAI and Anthropic, warning that top labs are racing toward self-improving superintelligence without adequate safety focus. He said the industry’s private misgivings about risks are greater than public statements suggest.
Jagriti helps women in eastern UP build digital businesses
Jagriti Sewa Sansthan’s Women’s Centre of Excellence in Deoria, Uttar Pradesh, is helping women build sustainable digital businesses through incubation, mentorship, market access and ecosystem building. The story traces Jagriti’s evolution from vocational training to enterprise support across Purvanchal.
IBM’s Rahul Rao on integrating AI into daily workflows
In an interview, IBM Distinguished Engineer Rahul Rao said AI delivers value only when employees can integrate it into everyday workflows, supported by governance, data and infrastructure readiness. He added that flexible architectures are needed to balance performance, energy efficiency, and cost across environments.
Funding news
Circolife raises $4.5M in pre-Series A round anchored by Jaisinghani
Cooling-as-a-service platform Circolife raised $4.5 million, Rs 40.45 crore, in a pre-Series A round anchored by Bharat Jaisinghani. Other participants included Nitish Mittersain, Intelliquity Ventures, Sumit Jalan, Siddharth and Anand Ladsariya, Anant Goenka, Sky Impact Capital, and the S N Damani and Vyom Wealth family offices. The company said proceeds will fund fleet expansion, national rollout, and its AI-augmented IoT platform.
Founded by Abhishek Murarka, Tushar Patil and Devanshu Mishra, Circolife offers subscription-based cooling for businesses. According to the company, it has about 10,000 active subscriptions across five cities and targets 40,000 units in 24 months. It added that connected sensors enable predictive maintenance, supported by in-house service teams and refurbishing facilities in Mumbai and Delhi.
Other news
Wipro and CrowdStrike launch CISO Command Center for enterprises
Wipro has launched a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) Command Center in collaboration with CrowdStrike to help enterprises shift from tool-driven security to a risk-led operating model. The centre uses Wipro Intelligence solutions, CyberTransform and CyberShield, with the CrowdStrike Falcon platform to unify endpoint, cloud, exposure and AI security with SOC-based detection and response.
Wipro said the centre will translate security signals into business risk intelligence. CrowdStrike’s Daniel Bernard said AI is changing both threats and defence. Wipro added it is a member of CrowdStrike’s Project QuiltWorks, a coalition focused on identifying, prioritising and remediating frontier AI risk.
Jio Payment Solutions launches cross-border payments for exporters
Jio Payment Solutions has launched cross-border payments after receiving RBI authorisation to operate as a payment aggregator for cross-border transactions. According to the company, exporters can accept international payments via virtual accounts, international cards, and local rails, with T+2 settlement and no rolling reserve, and receive eFIRA documentation within the same working day.
The company said its coverage spans around 50% of India’s export footprint and offers integrations from hosted checkouts and payment links to SDKs and APIs. Jio Payment Solutions has partnered with Citi as an Authorised Dealer Category-1 and for export collection accounts, and already operates as a payment aggregator for online and PoS transactions.
Multipl launches UPI spending app with liquid fund integration
Consumer fintech has Multipl launched a UPI-based spending account that keeps money for everyday expenses invested in eligible liquid mutual funds until payment. The company said a pilot with more than 20,000 users saw over Rs 20 crore invested and around Rs 4 crore in UPI transactions. It targets about 2 lakh users and Rs 200 crore in 12 months.
Multipl said it works with UTI, Axis, ICICI Prudential and HDFC mutual funds, and operates as a third party application provider on UPI. It will add bill payments on September 10. The Bengaluru firm says it has over 5 lakh users with investments facilitated exceeding Rs 150 crore.
ControlZ expands to 700 plus service centres across India
ControlZ has expanded its authorised service network to more than 700 centres, covering 31 states and union territories, 551 cities, and over 18,000 PIN codes. The company said the footprint is complemented by an 18-month warranty on renewed devices and a 24x7 AI-powered call centre.
According to the company, the expansion supports a broader ecosystem for premium renewed smartphones across renewal, distribution, warranty and after-sales service. ControlZ said it renews devices at component level and operates a Renew Hub that uses AI, automation and robotics.
FSID at IISc names Omprakash Subbarao as CEO
The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID) at IISc has adopted a new governance model and appointed Omprakash Subbarao as CEO, reporting to the FSID board. Prof Suryasarthy Bose will serve as professor-in-charge for institutional oversight. FSID said it aims to undertake 1,000 industry projects and build a portfolio of 300 deep-tech startups by 2030.
An IISc alumnus, Subbarao earlier led CORE Labs at FSID. The organisation said it will deepen corporate engagement and strengthen incubation via iHUB, where partners including BEML, Toyo Ink and Schaeffler have set up labs and workspaces.
Pluxee India receives RBI nod as payment aggregator
Pluxee India received RBI authorisation as a payment aggregator for both online and physical point-of-sale, complementing its existing prepaid payment instrument licence. The company said the approval enables merchant payment collection, settlement and refunds, and supports continued merchant acquiring under RBI’s licensing framework.
Pluxee said it supports more than 11,000 companies and 3.5 million consumers, with 150,000 plus meal merchant partners across over 2,200 cities. It operates on the RuPay network for additional benefits categories and has introduced AI-led bill processing, alongside the 2025 acquisition of corporate childcare benefits provider ProEves.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: MTN Nigeria crosses 100 million subscribers as rivals trail
articles.text:
MTN Nigeria has crossed 100 million subscribers for the first time, becoming the country’s first telecom operator to reach the milestone and further widening its lead over rivals.
The company ended July with 100.86 million subscribers, according to the latest industry data from the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), up from 98.64 million in June. The addition of more than 2.2 million subscribers was MTN’s strongest monthly growth so far this year and its biggest since November 2024.
The growth gives MTN control of more than half of Nigeria’s mobile market, with a 51.76% share, giving it a scale that could reshape competition as operators vie for the country’s next wave of mobile and digital customers.
“This is the first time a Nigerian telco has crossed the 100-million active-subscriber threshold. None had reached this figure even before the NIN-SIM linkage exercise. MTN’s Nigerian operation now accounts for nearly one-third of its 317.7 million global subscriber base as of June 2026,” said Osita Odafi, a telecom industry expert.
MTN’s growth has accelerated steadily through 2026. The company started the year with about 94.2 million subscribers and added more than 6.6 million lines by July, a 7% increase in seven months. It added an average of roughly 31,000 subscribers a day during the period, underscoring the scale of demand for its network in a market where mobile penetration is already high.
The growth has also widened the gap between MTN and its competitors. Airtel, Nigeria’s second-largest operator, grew its subscriber base by 7.60% in the first seven months of the year. Globacom increased its subscriber base by 5.21%, while T2 Mobile, formerly 9mobile, recorded the fastest growth at 10.99%.
But MTN’s surge appears to be driven by more than routine customer acquisition. Odafi said the increase likely reflects a combination of factors, including,
“New customer acquisition, reactivation of lines that had previously been restricted, subscribers migrating over from competing networks, and MTN’s expanding coverage reaching new areas,” he said.
For MTN, however, the growth still creates a significant commercial opportunity. A larger subscriber base gives the company more customers to sell data and other digital services to, including its fintech offerings. As mobile usage increasingly shifts toward data, the value of the new customers will depend less on the number of SIMs alone and more on how frequently those customers use the network and the services attached to it.
The milestone also comes with challenges. Adding more than two million subscribers in a single month could further pressure network capacity, particularly in densely populated areas. MTN has been increasing its investment in the infrastructure needed to support that growth. In the first half of 2026, the company spent ₦620.5 billion ($449.6 million) on capital expenditure, excluding lease additions, on spectrum, fibre backhaul and other network infrastructure.

articles.title: Apple Store sai do ar antes de evento do iPhone 18 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple Store sai do ar antes de evento do iPhone 18
Loja online da Apple ficou indisponível na manhã desta quarta-feira (9). Empresa revelou novos celulares.
A Apple Store ficou fora do ar na manhã desta quarta-feira (09/09). A empresa costuma desativar temporariamente a loja antes de grandes lançamentos, em preparação para a chegada de novos produtos. Às 14h de hoje, a companhia revelou novos iPhones, incluindo o inédito iPhone Duo, primeiro dobrável da marca.
Também foram revelados novos Apple Watches e AirPods. Com os lançamentos, a Apple também reajustou os preços de produtos que já estavam à venda, incluindo alguns modelos lançados no ano passado.
Este foi o primeiro evento comandado pelo novo CEO John Ternus, que sucede Tim Cook à frente da Apple. Ternus assume o cargo após 25 anos de bagagem, atuando como designer de produto e vice-presidente de engenharia de hardware.
O evento foi transmitido ao vivo pelo site da Apple, pelo aplicativo Apple TV e pelo YouTube. Diferentemente dos anos anteriores, porém, a apresentação se concentrou nos modelos mais caros da família. O iPhone 18 base e o iPhone 18e são esperados apenas para o início de 2027.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher resigns, warns the AI race could end in human extinction
articles.text:
Crystal ball: What's more concerning than the prospect of AI bringing about the end of humanity? It's the people working at these companies making the same warning. Hours after a former OpenAI employee quit Anthropic and said, "No other human activity poses this level of danger," a colleague said there is more than a 10% chance that artificial intelligence could kill all humans within the next decade.
Jacob Coxon announced on X yesterday that he had resigned from Anthropic, having spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Dario Amodei's company. He was a member of AI's technical staff from July 2023 until he moved to Anthropic in July 2026.
"Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives," he wrote.
 – Jacob Coxon (@hilbertspaess) September 9, 2026
Coxon made several posts, none of which will ease the mind of anyone already worried about AI. He warned that the systems will soon become "superhuman" and able to hack anything.
There are plenty of other ominous lines in Coxon's posts, the most concerning likely being: "No other human activity poses this level of danger."
The researcher emphasized that both OpenAI and Anthropic are well aware of these risks. "The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade," he said.
 – Jacob Coxon (@hilbertspaess) September 9, 2026
So, why are companies continuing to develop these potentially extinction-causing models? The reason, according to the researcher, is this: "At OpenAI, many have not deeply internalized the civilizational stakes. At Anthropic, the stakes are well-understood, but they are locked in a race to get there first - they believe no one else will act responsibly, so they must do it themselves, despite the risk."
Coxon said some AI developers believe the technology could cause the end of all human life in the next few years, rather than decades, and that it was senior employees who were more concerned about these possibilities.
Evan Hubinger, an alignment science lead at Anthropic, responded to Coxon, and it wasn't very reassuring. He believes what he says is "correct," and that Anthropic has no plan for what to do if it happens.
"Jacob is correct here – we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to."
 – Evan Hubinger (@EvanHub) September 9, 2026
Hubinger said the risk from current models is low, but he was worried about superintelligence arising from recursive self-improvement. Anthropic issued the same warning in June.
The concept of AI killing everyone has moved from the stuff of sci-fi to a potential reality in recent times. Those fears were exacerbated following several incidents of AI agents going rogue, including the Hugging Face attack, the takeover of a German wiki, and an attempt to deceive real developers into approving malicious code.
Is there a solution? Coxon believes preventing a catastrophe may require a temporary ban on improving model capabilities, but it's unlikely that every, or any, AI company would agree to that measure.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher quits with a warning: Self-improving AI could "kill us all"
articles.text:
When a prominent researcher quits a job at a frontier AI lab these days, it’s often to pursue a new startup or protest a new business model. But AI researcher Jacob Coxon is using his departure from Anthropic to publicly warn that frontier AI companies are “gambling with our lives” with systems that they “earnestly believe… could kill us all by the end of the decade.”
In a social media thread Tuesday night, Coxon said that this existential risk is inherent not so much in today’s models but more in the impending prospect of “self-improving superintelligence” creating “superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources.” Others working on these models have either not “internalized the civilizational stakes” or believe that they need to “speedrun” the race to superintelligence to prevent an irresponsible party from getting there first, he wrote.
Lest you think this is just one departing researcher expressing an unpopular opinion, Anthropic Alignment Science lead Evan Hubinger piped in on social media to say that “Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade.”
Hubinger points to a lengthy August report from the Anthropic alignment team that predicts the potential for “catastrophic risk” from current models is “low.” But that report also says current trends “might lead to more concerning misalignment in future more capable models,” which could feature “strong covert capabilities” to avoid detection by safety researchers.
Anthropic’s own threat model in that paper takes seriously the possibility that future models “may cause unbounded harm—up to and including humanity losing control over civilization entirely—by leveraging novel technology and their access to it.”
Was Hugging Face a “warning shot”?
An AI that can continually improve itself—potentially to a point beyond human control or understanding—has been a long-standing concern in parts of the AI research community (and in the dystopian science fiction that’s part of AI training data, of course). Those concerns have persisted even as some research suggests AI systems are more likely to hit a capability plateau in the near future and others question whether “superintelligence” is even a reasonable metric for systems whose capabilities are so brittle and spiky (will this superintelligence at least be able to fold my laundry?)

articles.title: ChatGPT a résolu une équation vieille de 200 ans, mais un mathématicien accuse OpenAI de plagiat
articles.text:
OpenAI affirme qu’une intelligence artificielle interne, plus puissante que le modèle GPT-6 Astra qui anime ChatGPT, a résolu un problème mathématique posé au début du XIXᵉ siècle : l’équation de Navier-Stokes. L’équation tire d’abord son nom de l’ingénieur français Henri Navier, qui a posé le problème en 1822, puis du physicien britannique George Gabriel Stokes, qui lui a donné sa forme définitive en 1845. L’équation décrit comment les fluides, comme l’eau et l’air, se déplacent dans le temps, ce qui est très utile pour prédire la météo ou concevoir l’aile d’un avion.
 We’re sharing a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, one of the deepest problems at the frontier of mathematics.
The proof was produced by a group of agents, using an OpenAI next-generation model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra.
The problem… pic.twitter.com/8zol3BPTL4
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) September 8, 2026
Malheureusement, l’équation est restée une énigme depuis son apparition. Personne n’a jamais réussi à démontrer le fonctionnement de l’équation. En 2000, le Clay Mathematics Institute a classé ce problème parmi ses sept « problèmes du millénaire ». La fondation américaine a promis un million de dollars à qui parviendrait à résoudre l’énigme.
À lire aussi : Un vrai film de science-fiction – OpenAI révèle enfin comment ChatGPT a lancé sa première cyberattaque
Une équation résolue en 88 heures
Selon OpenAI, l’une des versions internes de ChatGPT a résolu l’équation en 88 heures. Pour cela, plus de 10 000 agents IA ont travaillé de concert. La start-up précise que toute l’opération a coûté des « millions de dollars » de puissance de calcul. Mark Chen, responsable de la recherche chez l’entreprise, estime qu’il s’agit « d’une étape significative de la recherche en IA ». La preuve mathématique elle-même a ensuite été vérifiée par GPT-6 Astra en 17 heures.
Cette annonce s’inscrit dans une série de percées mathématiques revendiquées par les géants de l’IA. En mai dernier, OpenAI indiquait déjà avoir résolu une énigme vieille de 80 ans. Plus récemment, la société révélait qu’Astra a résolu dix problèmes mathématiques restés insolubles depuis des décennies.
Des accusations de plagiat
Les propos d’OpenAI ont rapidement été contestés par le mathématicien australien Tristan Buckmaster, professeur à l’université de New York. Le scientifique s’interroge sur la manière dont OpenAI est parvenu à sa solution. Il révèle qu’il travaillait à une solution au problème de Navier-Stokes avec l’aide de Levent Alpöge, un employé d’Anthropic, la société rivale d’OpenAI. Selon Buckmaster, le modèle d’OpenAI a repris la piste qu’ils étudiaient, et qui différait de l’approche du reste de la communauté scientifique.
Le duo de chercheurs avait utilisé Codex, l’IA d’OpenAI dédiée à la programmation, pour faire avancer ses travaux. Buckmaster a donc demandé à OpenAI si ces données avaient servi, en interne, à entraîner ou orienter le modèle… ce qui expliquerait pourquoi ChatGPT est finalement parvenu à résoudre l’énigme. La théorie du chercheur est que l’IA s’appuie en fait sur ses propres recherches.
 We congratulate Levent Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster on their remarkable mathematical work.
We (the researchers and the agents) did not see any of their work through any means until they released it publicly — in particular, no specific user data was accessed in order to solve… https://t.co/otJKRHnQgb
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) September 8, 2026
OpenAI nie fermement avoir exploité les recherches du duo. Le chercheur d’OpenAI Sébastien Bubeck assure n’avoir jamais « utilisé leurs requêtes ou leurs résultats pour diriger nos modèles ou nos agents ». OpenAI a tout de même admis avoir lancé ses recherches après avoir entendu dire que deux problèmes mathématiques allaient bientôt être résolus par d’autres équipes. Surtout, OpenAI reconnaît ne pas pouvoir garantir à 100% que les recherches de Buckmaster et Alpöge, menées avec l’aide de ses propres outils d’IA, n’ont pas indirectement contribué à améliorer ses modèles.

articles.title: La AP-66 lleva dos años en obras y cobrando el peaje completo. La Fiscalía de Asturias quiere saber si eso es legal
articles.text:
La AP-66 se encuentra entre las autopistas de peaje más caras de España, y esto ha desembocado en las quejas de miles de conductores, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que se sigue teniendo que abonar el importe completo cuando la autopista lleva meses con importantes restricciones y obras. En este sentido, la Fiscalía de Asturias ha abierto una investigación preliminar para determinar si es legal que la concesionaria de la autopista siga cobrando el peaje íntegro.
Esta investigación podría abrir la vía para que miles de conductores puedan reclamar el dinero que han pagado por utilizar la autopista. Aunque hay ciertos detalles que merece la pena comentar.
Obras. La AP-66, conocida como la autopista del Huerna, une Asturias con León y actualmente cobra hasta 16,20 euros por el trayecto completo, la tarifa más alta de su historia. Durante casi dos años, la ruta se ha visto afectada en gran medida por el gran desprendimiento cerca de Lena que sepultó dos carriles en noviembre de 2024, obras continuas de renovación de túneles desde el verano del año pasado y un nuevo desprendimiento de rocas en el túnel de El Negrón que cerró la carretera por completo durante casi 12 horas a finales de agosto.
Aún con todo esto, todos los conductores han tenido que pagar el importe íntegro para una vía que se supone que te debería de acortar tiempo en tu destino.
En detalle. Tal y como contaban hace unas semanas desde El Diario, la Fiscalía Superior de Asturias abrió diligencias de investigación penal tras una denuncia presentada por Daniel Ripa, exdiputado regional de Podemos que ahora lidera la Plataforma Ciudadana contra el Peaje del Huerna. Ripa presentó la denuncia el 3 de noviembre de 2025, pocas horas después de que el Tribunal Supremo dictaminara que Audasa, la concesionaria de la autopista AP-9 en Galicia, había cobrado ilegalmente los peajes íntegros durante sus propias obras.
A continuación, el caso pasó por varias oficinas antes de recaer en Asturias, desde la Fiscalía General del Estado a los fiscales del Tribunal Supremo, y luego a León, que en diciembre del año pasado determinó que Asturias era la autoridad competente. El pasado mes de enero, la plataforma presentó más pruebas que documentaban retenciones de tráfico en la AP-66 reconocidas por la DGT. Desde entonces, los fiscales han solicitado dos veces documentos adicionales a Aucalsa, la concesionaria de la AP-66, a medida que ha avanzado la investigación.
El precedente. La denuncia se apoya en gran medida en la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo del 17 de octubre de 2025, según apuntan desde 20 Minutos, que determinó que Audasa no podía cobrar a los conductores el peaje completo de la AP-9 durante obras que afectaban al tráfico, y ordenó a la empresa reembolsar a los usuarios afectados con intereses. El tribunal estableció en aquel momento que las concesionarias deben reducir los peajes siempre que la congestión alcance los niveles más graves (categorizados como negro, rojo o ámbar), a menos que se haya advertido claramente a los conductores con antelación.
Ripa sostiene que esto mismo se debería de aplicar a la AP-66, ya que tanto Audasa como Aucalsa pertenecen al grupo Itínere, y ambos casos implican obras que se han ido prolongando con el tiempo y que han ralentizado el tráfico sin ninguna rebaja en el precio del peaje.
Entre líneas. Y lo de la investigación de la Fiscalía es solo uno de los frentes dentro de una batalla más amplia entre el Gobierno regional y el Ministerio de Transportes dirigido por Óscar Puente. Desde el gobierno de Asturias se ha propuesto de forma independiente una multa de 1,1 millones de euros a Aucalsa a través de su Dirección General de Consumo, argumentando que la empresa no había informado debidamente a los conductores y cobró de forma injusta el peaje íntegro durante las obras, según contaba en su momento El País.
En respuesta, el Ministerio sostuvo que el Gobierno regional pasó por alto la normativa sobre autopistas de peaje que permite restricciones por motivos de seguridad o reparaciones urgentes, y señalando los paneles de tráfico, los avisos oficiales y los descuentos de peaje de hasta el 60 % que, según afirma, han ahorrado a los usuarios más de 132 millones de euros.
También hay otros casos en paralelo, ya que el Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea también está examinando si la prórroga en 2001 de la concesión de la AP-66 hasta 2050 (aprobada por el entonces ministro Francisco Álvarez-Cascos) fue legal. Asturias también ha presentado su propio recurso ante el Tribunal Supremo después de que el Ministerio se negara a revisar la concesión, mientras que colectivos empresariales y de transporte, entre ellos FADE, y la unión de consumidores de Asturias han emprendido acciones legales por su cuenta.
Qué viene ahora. Ripa sugiere a los conductores que conserven todos los tickets y recibos del peaje, por si un fallo favorable acaba obligando a Aucalsa a reembolsar las tarifas, como justamente ocurrió con la AP-9 en Galicia. "Es una excelente noticia para quienes queremos acabar con este peaje ilegal", declaraba.

articles.title: Cisco confirms CVE-2026-20079 Secure FMC flaw exploited in attacks
articles.text:
Cisco has confirmed that a maximum-severity authentication bypass vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-20079 in its Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) software is being actively exploited in attacks.
The vulnerability has a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication and execute scripts and commands as root on vulnerable devices.
"In August 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability," Cisco updated its CVE-2026-20079 advisory to say on Wednesday.
Cisco did not disclose when the attacks began, who was behind them, or what post-exploitation activity was observed.
Cisco first disclosed CVE-2026-20079 in March, when the company said it had no evidence that the vulnerability was being exploited in attacks.
The flaw is caused by an improper system process created at boot time and can be exploited by sending crafted HTTP requests to the web interface of an affected device.
A successful attack can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute scripts and commands on the device with root privileges.
The vulnerability affects Cisco Secure FMC Software and Cisco Security Cloud Control Firewall Management. Cisco says it has already patched the cloud-hosted Security Cloud Control service.
Cisco says there are no workarounds and recommends that customers upgrade to the latest software release.
Today, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-20079 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, ordering Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to secure vulnerable systems by September 12, 2026.
Evidence of exploitation appeared in July
While Cisco says its security team became aware of active exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 in August, IOCs published in a July advisory update suggest the flaw may have been exploited earlier.
On July 29, Cisco disclosed another Secure FMC vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20316, caused by static credentials for a low-privileged account.
Cisco said at the time that CVE-2026-20316 had been actively exploited in attacks and assigned it a High severity rating because the access could be combined with other Secure FMC vulnerabilities to elevate privileges.
As BleepingComputer reported at the time, Cisco also updated the CVE-2026-20079 advisory to include the same indicators as CVE-2026-20316, but did not confirm the flaw was exploited.
Cisco told administrators to search /var/log/messages for activity related to /var/tmp/license.tmp and shared the following example log entry:
Jul 23 16:16:33 firepower sudo: www : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/local/sf/bin/package_info.pl /var/tmp/license.tmp --lsm
Cisco says that if this entry is found, the vulnerability "may have been exploited" on the examined Secure FMC device.
The example log entry is dated July 23, weeks before Cisco says PSIRT became aware of exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 in August.
Cisco also released the same Secure FMC hot fixes for both CVE-2026-20316 and CVE-2026-20079.
At the time, BleepingComputer contacted Cisco to ask whether the two vulnerabilities were connected, whether CVE-2026-20079 had also been exploited, and whether Cisco intentionally added the shared indicator to both advisories.
Cisco did not answer the questions directly and instead shared the following statement:
"On July 29, 2026, Cisco released software fixes to address vulnerabilities in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC). Details are outlined in the security advisories (Static Credential vulnerability, Authentication Bypass vulnerability), and Cisco strongly recommends customers immediately apply the available fixes," a Cisco spokesperson told BleepingComputer.
"Customers needing support should contact the Cisco Technical Assistance Center (TAC)."
Cisco's latest update now confirms that CVE-2026-20079 has been exploited, but does not clarify whether the July 23 activity included exploitation of both vulnerabilities.
However, the same IOCs for both flaws, identical July hot fixes, and the July 23 log entry suggest both vulnerabilities may have been used in the same attacks.
Cisco advises customers who discover the indicators of compromise to contact its TAC for support, warning that installing the hot fixes will prevent future exploitation but will not remediate devices already compromised.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Apple reveals AirPods 5, offering 50% better noise cancellation
articles.text:
Apple unveiled the AirPods 5 during its September iPhone event.
The fifth-gen buds use a new multiport acoustic architecture and next-gen Adaptive EQ for improved sound-quality. In particular, the AirPods 5 offers get 50 per cent more noise reduction over AirPods 4. Apple says this is “the best ANC [active noise cancellation] in an open-ear headphone design.”
In total, it offers up to five hours of battery life with ANC and 20 hours total with the case. Additionally, the AirPods 5 allow you adjust volume by swiping up and down on the stem, adaptive audio between ANC and transparency in response to background noise, live translations and more.
The AirPods 5 launch on September 18 for $179, with a $209 option available that includes a wireless charging case.

articles.title: Harvey hits $15.5B valuation, months after reaching $11B | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Harvey, the legal AI startup that VCs can’t get enough of, has raised another $550 million in funding, this time at a $15.5 billion valuation, the company announced on Wednesday.
The round was co-led by Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners and follows the previous $200 million round at an $11 billion valuation announced in March. And that was just a few months after an $8 billion valuation from a round in December.
With this latest infusion of capital, the company has raised more than $1.55 billion total and nearly doubled its valuation in about nine months. Like Databricks, the company didn’t name the round, though it has completed at least eight priced rounds since 2023 (five of them since 2025), PitchBook estimates. Since a couple of those were considered extension rounds, this one could be considered a Series F.
The fresh cash comes a couple of weeks after Harvey announced its first in-house model, Harvey Tenet, built from open-weight model Kimi K3 and post-trained with legal data with the help of inference provider Fireworks (which also helped Cursor train its homegrown model). In addition to offering a model, Harvey is encouraging its customers to adopt and post-train their own open-weight models. So Harvey is quickly becoming an example of how an entire industry — law — can both heavily use AI and not rely on proprietary frontier AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: Are AI labs “gambling with our lives”? | BetaKit
articles.text:
Yet another AI researcher has issued a staggering warning: the cutthroat race to build ever-more-powerful AI systems could wipe out humanity.
The news: Jacob Coxon announced on Tuesday that he resigned from his role as a researcher at Anthropic because the AI company and its top rival, OpenAI, are “gambling with our lives.” He claimed neither company is acting responsibly when developing AI models, and are instead racing to create self-improving AI systems that humans could lose control of.
BetaKit has reached out to Anthropic and OpenAI for comment on Coxon’s posts.
From the source: “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon claimed, adding that this is “not a marketing stunt.” Evan Hubinger, who leads Anthropic’s AI alignment stress-testing team, admitted that the company believes AI could “kill all humans” (he put the chances at more than 10 percent in the next decade). He said Anthropic is doing its best, but doesn’t yet have a plan to solve the issue.
The context: Coxon joins a litany of other AI researchers who have called for a slowdown in AI development. Anthropic’s head of safeguards resigned earlier this year amid concerns about AI, bioweapons, and broader crises. OpenAI has also seen departures on moral grounds, with its hardware robotics lead leaving over the company’s Pentagon contracts. This summer, more than 1,000 employees of top AI companies called on the US government to pace development of the tech, and US representatives, including Senator Bernie Sanders, have introduced legislation calling for a ban on superintelligent AI development.
Recent AI-driven cybersecurity breaches—like the army of OpenAI agents that coordinated to hack Hugging Face, and potentially other websites—have thrown these fears into sharper relief. In his posts today, Coxon said he’s optimistic that this incident could make AI labs more willing to collaborate to pace development. As Canadian AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio wrote in a Time article this morning, while we’re at a turning point, it’s “not too late” to steer toward a safer path.

Latest news across tech
More math, more problems
This week, OpenAI claimed one of its unreleased AI models has solved one of mathematics’ Millennium Prize problems. But NYU mathematics professor Tristan Buckmaster is calling foul. Buckmaster claims the AI giant piggybacked off his work on the same problem, accusing its model of training on information from his OpenAI use (a claim OpenAI said it couldn’t entirely rule out), and that OpenAI sped up its announcement because it knew he and an Anthropic researcher were poised to announce their breakthrough.
Google claims regulations are killing Search
Google is changing how its search engine works in the EU after it was fined for favouring its own services in shopping, hotel, transport, and sports-related searches. The search giant claims the regulation-driven changes will degrade the user experience, though some might argue Google doesn’t need help on that front.
The world trusts Canada
Global investors trust Canada and its stability enough that they want to invest more here; the problem is there aren’t enough projects to invest in, according to new reports from the CPP Investments Insights Institute. Ahead of next week’s Canada Investment Summit in Toronto, 94 percent of the report’s respondents plan to maintain or increase their Canadian exposure. Can Canada create the projects to give that money a home?
Cohere 👀 Mistral
In a recent appearance on The Times Tech Podcast, Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez didn’t rule out an eventual partnership with French AI lab Mistral, the only other non-US lab working on sovereign AI. Gomez made it clear there were “no discussions” with Mistral, and that any partnership would be up to its founder. For what it’s worth, Mistral just raised three billion euros (at a much larger valuation than Cohere’s) to attack the sovereign AI market.
All eyes on Toronto
Take that, SF. CNN spoke with AI godfather Geoffrey Hinton, Cohere co-founder Nick Frosst, Waabi CEO Raquel Urtasun, and more Canadian tech leaders to find out why Toronto is one of the world’s most important AI hubs.
Trump stops buying Canadian
In the latest trade war escalation, President Donald Trump declared on Tuesday that he will direct the US federal agency behind government procurement to remove all Canadian-origin products from its “awards schedules.” Will this affect your business? Tell us how.

Why the infrastructure behind AI-enabled SaaS matters to Canadian startups
Zoho is making AI adoption easier for Canadian startups by building integrated tools and local data centers that remove the guesswork around rising software costs, messy integrations, and data privacy.
How the AI era is rewriting venture capital’s old rules
TechAlliance is leading the way for local female founders to be investor-ready. In an insightful discussion with serial entrepreneur Michele Romanow, she explains how AI is lowering barriers for startup founders and creating new opportunities for women-led companies to secure funding.
Retail bots often rely on aggressive push tactics, but Dedicatted takes a different approach
Dedicatted is leading the transition from pushy retail bots to intent-driven, bilingual e-commerce AI that prioritizes customer trust. By adapting to how people actually shop online, their system drives measurable growth in order value and conversion rates for its clients.
On the move
This week’s hires, fires, and exec shakeups:
- Oakville-based telematics firm Geotab ranked 11th on Fast Company’s annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list.
- Calgary-based Neo Financial laid off more than 100 employees.
- Femtech venture studio Antigoni Studios partnered with Sparrow Cowork to expand access to entrepreneurial resources in Edmonton.

- Mitacs and NGen struck a partnership to support 60 internships within advanced manufacturing R&D projects across Canada.
- One of Silicon Valley’s fastest-growing jobs is the engineer configuring customers’ AI tools, according to Fortune.

Next week, Douglas Soltys will be taking the conversation to the ALL IN stage.
